passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text:
Oh, hi! Isn't this a great shot? I love my S.E.L.F.I.E. camera!

Do you want me to make you one, too? I only need a few parts!

For the strap, I'll need a Russet Belt from one of the armor merchants in Stormwind.

I've already ordered more housings, you're welcome to take one, you just have to find where my shipment ended up!

Oh, and a Standard Scope, most any engineer can make you one of those.

Ok, are you ready for a little photography action?!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text: Look at this shot? I could shoot here all day! Did you get those parts yet?

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text:
Great! I've just gotta put this box here, and jam this part in here... and done!

Here's your new S.E.L.F.I.E. cam, enjoy!

passages.title: A Flickering of Hope
passages.text:
This pervasive darkness continues to cast shadows over our fields, hindering our harvests.

Check with Keyrra Flamestonge and see if you can help restore some order.

passages.title: A Flickering of Hope
passages.text: There is always work to be done, <name>. Your assistance in illuminating additional keyflames would instill hope and allow many here to return to work.

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
<A flyer, carried by the wind, flaps into your hands.>

Fancy yourself a collector, trader, or adventurer? 

We've travelled all over Azeroth collecting goods of the finest quality for someone exactly like you!

Visit one of our outposts in Stormwind or Dornogal and browse all the latest goods!

--T&W Trading Post

<You squint to read the fine print.>

Be sure to present this flyer for some extra Trader's Tender!

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
Welcome to the Tradin' Post! 

We've got goods from all over Azeroth for ye to collect. Would ye like to take a look?

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
Now that ye've visted the shop and taken a look at our wares, here's a few more Trader's Tender for bringin' in that flyer.

If you want to keep earnin' tender, then check out the Traveler's Log portion of the Adventure Guide to see what activities ye can do. Complete enough activities and we'll reward you with tender and other amazing items.

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
<A flyer, carried by the wind, flaps into your hands.>

Rare antiquities from every corner of Azeroth! Fine goods fit for any taste!

You will not find these unique treasures anywhere else, friend.

Come see us at one of our outposts in Orgrimmar or Dornogal and gaze in wonder upon the mysteries in store for you!

--Zen'shiri Trading Post

<You squint to read the fine print.>

Be sure to present this flyer for some extra Trader's Tender!

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
Welcome to the Trading Post. 

We have goods from all over Azeroth here for your collectin'. Please, take a look.

passages.title: Tour the Trading Post
passages.text:
Ah, ya brought in one of our flyers! As promised, here's some Trader's Tender ya can use in our shop.

If ya want to keep earning tender, then check out the Traveler's Log portion of the Adventure Guide to see what activities ya can do. Complete enough activities and we'll reward ya with tender and other amazing items.

passages.title: Report to the Trading Post
passages.text: <The glint of a distant object catches your eye. You suddenly remember that you have tender to collect for use at T&W Trading Post.>

passages.title: Report to the Trading Post
passages.text: Hope ye like this month's collection of new and exotic wares, <name>.

passages.title: Glow in the Dark
passages.text:
Codswallop! Peevish has run off again. He is assigned to this post but is never here!

I heard him screaming from the nearby cave. He must have tried to hide in there.

Take my torch and go to the Coldshadow Cave. Find Peevish along with the bottles of Dauntless Draught he stole. He can desert his post if he wants, but I won't let him take the drinks!

passages.title: Glow in the Dark
passages.text: Have you found "Peevish" Paeton Berncort and the bottles of Dauntless Draught he took with him?

passages.title: Glow in the Dark
passages.text:
I didn't anticipate Peevish would muster the courage to return, but at least you recovered the Draught. 

We'll raise a toast and wish him luck in that cave.

passages.title: Work It
passages.text:
The Trial of Style gives us the opportunity to look good, <class>.

The camera makes sure we keep looking good. 

So focus on me and my camera, follow my directions and I'll make sure you look fantastic!

passages.title: Work It
passages.text:
Focus on me and follow my directions. 

I'll make sure you look great.

passages.title: Work It
passages.text:
The camera doesn't lie, <name>. 

You are one stylish <class>.

passages.title: The Trial of Style
passages.text:
Well, that's certainly an... interesting look, <class>.

Me? Judgmental? Certainly not. However, I'm curious what others would think of it.

You should speak to the Transmogrifier over there and enter the Trial of Style.

We'll see what public opinion says about your choice in garb.

passages.title: The Trial of Style
passages.text:
Ugh, I'm so bored.

Did you complete the Trial of Style yet?

passages.title: The Trial of Style
passages.text:
That's mildly impressive.

Mildly.

Off with you now. I'm tired of looking at you.

passages.title: Fashion Week
passages.text:
Ah, the Trial of Style is upon us, <class>. 

The outfits, the creativity, the elegance of the Trial are truly a sight to see.

Speak to a Trial of Style Envoy to learn more about the event.

A word of warning, those envoys can be... challenging to deal with.

passages.title: Fashion Week
passages.text:
You really think you're ready for the Trial of Style?

In that?

passages.title: Shadows of Flavor
passages.text:
I've set out to create a meal that transcends the ordinary, one that even the emperor wouldn't turn away.

I require ingredients from the darkest of shadows to craft this extraordinary meal. Many consider these ingredients forbidden, but they will become a harmony of light and shadow in my hands.

Please assist me by harvesting the following ingredients: Shadowblind Grouper, Dark-Nurtured Scallions, and a Vial of Twilight Spice.

passages.title: Shadows of Flavor
passages.text: Have you found all of the ingredients?

passages.title: Shadows of Flavor
passages.text: Now the magic happens. Please sample this creation for yourself.

passages.title: The Kalimdor Cup Circuit
passages.text:
The Riders of Azeroth have learned much from us, and now we test their mettle, as well as yours, skyrider!

My bronze colleagues have traveled to Kalimdor to create new challenges. They await you with many races across the continent.

Are you up to the task?

passages.title: The Kalimdor Cup Circuit
passages.text: Have you taken wing today?

passages.title: The Kalimdor Cup Circuit
passages.text: You lead the way among your fellow dragonriders! As the Kalimdor Cup continues, find other races there and prove you are a cut above the rest.

passages.title: Defender of the Flame
passages.text:
The Expedition forces face formidable adversaries.

Drawn like moths to our keyflames, creatures of all types are intent on snuffing out the light and thwarting our rebuilding efforts.

Please help us defeat two of the most menacing denizens that threaten our keyflames. Together, we can drive back this darkness.

passages.title: Defender of the Flame
passages.text: Have you eliminated the threats?

passages.title: Defender of the Flame
passages.text: Excellent work, that is two less threats to deal with!

passages.title: Right Between the Gyro-Optics
passages.text:
My husband Ezgi loves those harvesters, but I don't trust them, and now you can see why!

The lights go out, and they all start trying to kill us!

You want to help me sort this out?

I'm a crack shot with a rifle. You mark the target, and I'll start shooting!

passages.title: Right Between the Gyro-Optics
passages.text: Ezgi is going to be upset, but you and I did what needed to be done.

passages.title: Tater Trawl
passages.text:
Harvesting in this area has become a challenge, with crazed Harvesters destroying most of our crops. There are potatoes to be found if you look closely.

If you light the harvest torches, you might uncover some potatoes hiding in the shadows. 

Using those lights, gather as many potatoes as you can. Every bit helps in these trying times.

passages.title: Tater Trawl
passages.text: Have you found any spuds?

passages.title: Tater Trawl
passages.text: This is perfect. We love fried potato fingers, we're going to cook up some of those tonight!

passages.title: Lost in Shadows
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>. I find myself in a dire situation. 

Some fresh recruits and I were on patrol in these lands when our torches went out, leaving us utterly lost and disoriented.

I found safety in this house, but most of the recruits fled, confused into the darkness. 

Will you help me locate them? I have a spare Patrol Torch. The mere sight of it should rally them to your side.

passages.title: Lost in Shadows
passages.text: Have you found the recruits?

passages.title: Lost in Shadows
passages.text: The time spent with you is much greater training than I could ever provide these recruits. One of them will remain here to aid you further.

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! You just missed Lord Andestrasz. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, dragonrider!

passages.title: Force Your Way
passages.text:
Even with the general gone, it's not going to be easy getting out of here. This place is infested.

I know I'm hiding it well, but I'm not exactly feeling my best. I'm not sure I'll be much help in this state.

You're going to have to clear a path for us.

passages.title: Force Your Way
passages.text: Say what you will, but you do meet the most interesting company while imprisoned.

passages.title: Force Your Way
passages.text:
In my defense, they disarmed me. And envenomed me. Also, does this look infected to you?

Anyway, if not for all that, I would have helped. You have my word.

passages.title: Scrappy Straggler
passages.text:
If someone got left behind, we need to do something about that.

I hate to say it, but these people need someone to protect them here. I have to stay.

Find this straggler. And while you're at it, take a peek behind enemy lines. See if you can find anything useful.

passages.title: Scrappy Straggler
passages.text: The others all made it to safety, right?

passages.title: Scrappy Straggler
passages.text:
I definitely had everything under control.

<Flynn winces.>

But... I'll admit, this venom is dulling my otherwise lightning-quick reflexes, <name>.

passages.title: Dalaran's Most Distressed
passages.text:
I don't trust this big bug at all. He let me lay there ages without saying anything!

But if he wants to give us access to Siegehold, let's use it. I saw some other people dragged away into other parts of the base. I don't think they're eating them. It looks more like they're transporting them somewhere.

Let's gather them up, make a prisoner convoy, and roll on out. Find me outside!

passages.title: Dalaran's Most Distressed
passages.text:
Wow... this is a LOT of people.

But they're all miserable. Fortunately, that's just the flavor we need to sell my idea.

This could work.

passages.title: Just Act Casual
passages.text:
It's time to get outta here with the prisoners and those pheromones. I've found some convincing chains, since we have such a big group. Long as everybody stays in character, our chances look good. 

We've only got General Anub'azal's marker scent goop for you and I, so we'll be the drones with permission. You do all the talkin', while I mind the cart. I hope this works.

Lead us through the gate, <name>!

passages.title: Just Act Casual
passages.text: We just need to make it out of the entrance. I'll figure it out from there.

passages.title: Just Act Casual
passages.text: Let's take a quick breath. We didn't lose anyone, did we?

passages.title: To Rambleshire
passages.text:
There's word of troubles in the village of Rambleshire, at the base of Thunderhead Peak. 

Can't abide the place myself. Always wet and rumbling.

But Rooktender Lufsela thought it worth a look, however, seeing as how the birds fancy the moss that the village produces. She's still green though, and might just need a hand.

passages.title: To Rambleshire
passages.text:
Otwin sent you? Probably misses my help brushing out the rooks. But there's something amiss here in Rambleshire.

There should be a storm overhead. Been visible from Dornogal for as long as I can remember. Without that storm, I fear the local mosswool operation is in trouble.

passages.title: Power Predators
passages.text:
Thunderhead Peak normally boasts a perpetual storm from which the local mosswools draw energy. Without it, the poor dears look to be listless and near dead on their feet. That makes them easy pickings for predators.

To get moss production back on track, we'll need to get to the bottom of the missing storm. But first we need to beat back these predators before they turn the mosswools to gravel.

passages.title: Power Predators
passages.text: Please do what you can for the poor mosswools.

passages.title: Power Predators
passages.text:
That should buy the ranchers and their flocks some time while we figure out what's going on with the missing storm. No storm means no moss, which means grumpy storm rooks.

According to the locals, the storm is born of two legendary rams butting heads atop Thunderhead Peak. They think one of them went missing, if you can believe that.

passages.title: Friends in Low Places
passages.text:
When we crashed, the nerubians were upon us in an instant. We would have lost nearly everyone we brought with us, had someone not intervened.

I do not know who--or what--stepped in on our behalf. But if there is even a shred of hope that we have allies in this place then we must seize upon it and refuse to let go.

passages.title: Friends in Low Places
passages.text: Ah! You survived. Excellent. You have much to do.

passages.title: Heroes Never Die
passages.text:
Damn it all! We were too hasty, and now my people are paying the price.

We were fools to think the nerubians wouldn't be prepared for an incursion. Arathi soldiers are made of stern stuff, but even they will struggle to walk off an airship crash.

I will keep everyone here safe. Please, go into the field and rescue as many people as you can.

passages.title: Heroes Never Die
passages.text: Make haste, <class>. Time is of the essence.

passages.title: Heroes Never Die
passages.text: I thank you, <name>, on behalf of those you saved. No one deserves to die alone in the dark, least of all in a place like this.

passages.title: For Naught, So Vial
passages.text:
Truthfully, I don't care what the nerubians are plotting. They are not the first upstart people seeking power, and they certainly won't be the last. The problem is how they're going about it. I fear that tampering with this Black Blood will threaten far more than the delicate ecosystems of Khaz Algar.

We must make sure that they never return to this pit again. Their equipment is still strewn throughout the pit. Destroy as much of it as you can manage.

passages.title: For Naught, So Vial
passages.text: The nerubians fled when those aberrations began appearing en masse, but I imagine they will try to come back for their ill-advised treasures. We need to make sure they have nothing to come back for.

passages.title: For Naught, So Vial
passages.text:
<Orweyna scowls.>

The nerubians are a bold people, but this seems extreme, even for them.

passages.title: Fear the Old Blood
passages.text:
This is not exactly the place for a long talk, so I will be brief.

These roots you see are part of something much greater than you know, and it is my job to protect them. 

If it isn't obvious to you already, this place is teeming with writhing Black Blood. If we do not act, it will spread deeper and further still.

You want allies? Fine. Help me cleanse this place and protect these roots, and I will at least hear you out.

passages.title: Fear the Old Blood
passages.text:
Between your sweat and my spellwork, we've managed to at least contain the problem to this blighted cavern.

Still, what a disaster. If this is what one cave of the stuff can do, I shudder to think what the nerubians might do with more of it.

passages.title: Slay the Saboteurs
passages.text:
The nerubians are everywhere, <name>.

There are too many for all of them to be solely crash survivors. I've seen others burrowing up from the ground. 

This Queensguard Zirix was laying in wait here to overwhelm us.

Let them know we are not easy prey. Cut them down!

passages.title: Slay the Saboteurs
passages.text: We need to thin their numbers if we are to survive this.

passages.title: Slay the Saboteurs
passages.text: Good work. And we've made progress as well. Perhaps now we can press forward.

passages.title: Erratic Artifacts
passages.text:
Dalaran housed many precious and powerful relics. Many of them were damaged in the crash and are now malfunctioning.

They must be destroyed!

Take this scroll. I have stored a shattering spell within it. Read the words aloud and its magic will be unleashed.

Report what you have done to Jaina when you are through. She will understand.

passages.title: Erratic Artifacts
passages.text: It pains me, but we have to destroy the malfunctioning relics!

passages.title: Erratic Artifacts
passages.text:
Destroying more of Dalaran seems unconscionable.

But you and Aethas did the right thing.

They were unstable, and we could not risk their power being used against us.

passages.title: Bring the Thunder
passages.text:
The nerubians will strike out in anger and pride--which is exactly what we want.

They will swarm the meadery soon, seeking to punish us for attacking their burrow. We will hold them here on the ground while you take to the skies. When Zirix appears to command his army, we will light the fuses.

Wenbrandt scrounged together some supplies we can use to corral the nerubians. Set them up quickly, and then we will get you on a stormrook. Go!

passages.title: Bring the Thunder
passages.text:
Zirix is dead. We did it. It is over. Baelgrim did it.

<She repeats the last phrase to herself over and over more quietly each time as if unable to process the event.>

passages.title: Return to the Coreway
passages.text:
We dealt a heavy blow to the nerubians. But Baelgrim...

<Adelgonn pauses to compose herself.>

He was infuriatingly rigid and we argued ceaselessly, but in the end... he was a defender of our people--all of them.

Baelgrim sacrificed himself to vouchsafe the Isle of Dorn from the nerubians. Everyone needs to know that--and we can't let the nerubians force our hand like that again.

Go back to Merrix in Dornogal. Tell him we will come soon. We just... need a moment here.

passages.title: Return to the Coreway
passages.text: How fares your sortie at the meadery?

passages.title: Return to the Coreway
passages.text: You are alive! But what of the others?

passages.title: Reforged Purpose
passages.text: That's all of them! Now, it's time to do my duty and recast these tools. Reforge them, and myself, into what I was meant to be: a proud machinist of the Ringing Deeps.

passages.title: Reforged Purpose
passages.text: I'm ready to do my part once again. I just need to reforge these old tools.

passages.title: Reforged Purpose
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough for all of your help. I lost my faith, but now, I have both my faith and my tools back.

I'm forever grateful to you.

passages.title: Frayed Legacy
passages.text:
Keep true, <race>t.

We of the Woldguard uphold an ancient promise to Freya to tend to these lands. Our edict is older than those wielded by the demagogues in Dornogal. Older than Dornogal itself.

However, not all lands have been tended equally. The leader of our order was to care for the basin nearby but we've not heard from them in many cycles.

I have sent a novice to investigate. Aid them and my order will be in your favor.

passages.title: Frayed Legacy
passages.text: This is not as this basin should be. We have much work to do.

passages.title: Invasive Cuisine
passages.text: <This rarely seen plant may be of use to Chef Dinaire.>

passages.title: Invasive Cuisine
passages.text: Umbral Eggplant might not be everyone's idea of a delicious food, but when I prepare it, it is a crowd favorite!

passages.title: A Candle in the Dark
passages.text:
Beledar has turned to Shadow, we must retreat back to Mereldar!

<Vaelisia looks towards Aelric Leid.>

I-- No. We need to destroy Aelric first.

Take him down, then we retreat.

passages.title: A Candle in the Dark
passages.text:
May the Light bless Faerin. 

I thought the Eternal Flame lost. 

I thought this was the end of hope, and the death of our people.

passages.title: The Final Front
passages.text:
Just before the kobyss attacked, we received word of a disturbance near Livia's Patience. Now we know the cause.

We... Light... We can't survive fighting on two fronts, <name>. We have to stop this, now.

passages.title: The Final Front
passages.text:
Flames, they tunnelled up through the lake bed.

Livia's Patience has already fallen.

passages.title: The Rise of the Reckoning
passages.text:
The Reckoning is ready!

Let's make these spiders pay. Blood for blood.

passages.title: The Rise of the Reckoning
passages.text: We will make the nerubians regret ever thinking they could push into our home!

passages.title: The Rise of the Reckoning
passages.text: What fools we are.

passages.title: Hose It Down
passages.text:
With the flame restored, you can see the extent of contamination to the fishing hole. Kobyss and frogs have left heaps of strange goo that pollutes the shoreline.

We need your help to clean up this gooey blight! 

I have a specially modified harvester equipped with a water barrel. Use this device to spray water on the goo piles and clean the shore of this contamination.

passages.title: Hose It Down
passages.text: Have you cleaned up the shoreline?

passages.title: Hose It Down
passages.text: Great work <name>, things will be a lot less messy around here now!

passages.title: Where the Light Touches
passages.text:
Many in Hallowfall will call you "outsider". I would call you friend. I would also ask for your help, if you are no stranger to combat. Desperate times forge strong friendships.

General Steelstrike ordered the army to fall back from the nerubian onslaught. In doing so, she abandoned a Lamplighter and many troops to the darkness. I may not be able to save them on my own, but with your help I may succeed.

If you're willing, ride with me or meet me there.

passages.title: Where the Light Touches
passages.text: Outsider! The nerubians took us by surprise. The army went into retreat when the wall was breached. I've been keeping them away from this tower, but I could certainly use your help.

passages.title: Tunnel Trouble
passages.text:
It's good to have new allies here. Together, we have much better chances of protecting this tower.

The nerubians have overwhelmed us. If we're going to have any chance against them, we need to destroy the burrows they're using to come under the Wall.

If you can handle that, we will survey the field from the top of the wall and meet you there.

passages.title: Tunnel Trouble
passages.text: Were you able to stop the nerubians from coming under the ground?

passages.title: Tunnel Trouble
passages.text: Excellent, <name>--if we don't have to worry about the nerubians stabbing us in the back, we can deal with those pouring through below.

passages.title: The Only Good Spider
passages.text:
adventurer, if we don't stem the tide of nerubians climbing up to us, nothing else will matter.

Their numbers are just too great.

We need to delay their onslaught to buy the people of Hallowfall time to prepare. The wall still serves as a very effective chokepoint.

Do what you can to thin their numbers.

passages.title: The Only Good Spider
passages.text: <name>, every nerubian you kill here could mean a life saved in Hallowfall, and aids the chances of our own success.

passages.title: The Only Good Spider
passages.text: This is a good start. There are still many more nerubians coming from below, but we must turn our attention to those already inside Hallowfall.

passages.title: For Their Eyes Only
passages.text:
We've fought the nerubians since we arrived, adventurer. Their attacks have not risen to this level in a long time.

These airship docks are clearly a target, but do they have any others? Is there a larger goal?

The nerubians carry shadecasters with orders from their queen. We need to learn what we can of their plans and intentions, and recovering a few of those shadecasters is the best way we can do so.

passages.title: For Their Eyes Only
passages.text: Have you found any of those shadecasters yet, <name>?

passages.title: For Their Eyes Only
passages.text: Final war? Ascension? Not as many answers as questions, <name>. But we at least have some pieces of the puzzle.

passages.title: A Lamplighter's Duty
passages.text:
Darkness has fallen. We can't rest yet. 

<Faerin gives you a weary smile, but there is a light in her eyes.>

The light from the tower will hold the worst dangers in the darkness at bay. It's my duty, as a Lamplighter, to keep all the towers blazing. 

My patrol takes me to Lorel's Crossing by air next. I would welcome you and Anduin at my side, for all our sakes.

passages.title: A Lamplighter's Duty
passages.text:
The kobyss have already been dragging innocent villagers to the shore! They'll drown them and eat them!

We have to save them!

passages.title: The Tunnel's End
passages.text:
So we're hearing more rumors about Taelloch. 

The town and its mine are responsible for ore production. Apparently, we haven't received shipments in weeks, and the town's foreman has disappeared. Now the High Speaker is discouraging anyone from traveling there.

That tells me we should investigate. And of course, if people are hurting, then we should help them.

passages.title: The Tunnel's End
passages.text: We have to find out what happened here.

passages.title: The Tunnel's End
passages.text:
Beasts inside?

The residents of Taelloch might need our help.

Help me keep an eye on Dagran, <name>. He's read a lot of stories about thrilling adventures, but he hasn't seen what we've seen. 

And something seems... off.

passages.title: Lights Out
passages.text:
Name's Aegor. I try to keep tabs on Lamplighters in the field and assess what areas of Hallowfall may be in need of their aid.

The dawntower fell dark at Velhan's Claim a few weeks ago. Based on what's been happening around Hallowfall, it's probably because of the rising tide of kobyss.

Lamplighters Taenar and Aemyra are heading there, but this might be more than even two Lamplighters together can handle. Will you meet them there and help them restore the light at Velhan's Claim?

passages.title: Lights Out
passages.text:
Pleased to meet you, <name>. I'm Taenar, and this is Aemyra.

The dawntower at Velhan's Claim went dark a while ago, and with all that's been happening, we're only just getting here to help.

We did some scouting, and it seems the area is overrun with kobyss. I imagine Velhan's holed up inside, instead of fighting them off.

Good thing for his people that we're here. And it's better still to have you along helping.

passages.title: Crash Recovery
passages.text:
A lot of things went wrong when the Indomitable crashed, adventurer. But the most upsetting one is that--when the order was finally given to make our way back to Mereldar, we couldn't honor our fallen comrades.

It seems the kobyss reanimated our fallen stalwarts, who now wander the Indomitable in a ghastly skeletal form.

Take back their tinderboxes. If we can deliver those to the Sacred Flame, they'll finally be free after all these years.

passages.title: Crash Recovery
passages.text: Did you find those tinderboxes, <name>?

passages.title: Crash Recovery
passages.text:
The flame burns for us all, <name>. I wish I could have saved them that night, but I'm glad we'll be able to honor their memories.

It's what we all would want, if it happened to us.

passages.title: Cage, Match
passages.text:
When we were scouting before you arrived, we saw a lot of cages set up around Velhan's Claim. Typically, the kobyss use these to hold their victims until they're needed for a ritual sacrifice.

Those sacrifices lead to... lots of other dark activities. Not the least of which is eating the victims.

Let's get ahead of all that. Take my torch, and destroy the cages, so we don't have to see that happen to anyone from Velhan's Claim.

passages.title: Cage, Match
passages.text: Have you dealt with those cages yet? The citizens of Velhan's Claim won't be safe until you do.

passages.title: Cage, Match
passages.text:
Good work, <name>. Without their cages, the kobyss won't be able to take prisoners.

No prisoners means no foul rituals, and preventing those gives us a much better chance of saving the people at Velhan's Claim.

passages.title: If It Leads, It Bleeds
passages.text:
Everything rises and falls on leadership, adventurer. With a good leader, a unit can achieve almost anything. With a bad leader, chaos ensues and success moves out of reach. I've seen that first-hand.

Without leaders, the kobyss siege will break like a wave and everything else we do here becomes easier. I've seen three kobyss who seem to be leading the others--let me mark their locations on your map.

Deal with them, and we'll be much more able to help Velhan's Claim.

passages.title: If It Leads, It Bleeds
passages.text: Did you find their leaders? They look strong, but I'm sure you're up to the task.

passages.title: If It Leads, It Bleeds
passages.text:
Excellent. That will put us and the kobyss on a more even footing. At least in terms of leadership.

They still outnumber us by a lot, but one thing at a time.

passages.title: Situational Awareness
passages.text:
Regardless of what history Taenar and Velhan have between them, we need to take care of the people here at Velhan's Claim.

adventurer, will you please check in with the families here? Let them know we're here to help.

See if they're worried or need anything. And reassure them that the Lamplighters will drive back the kobyss.

passages.title: Situational Awareness
passages.text: It's so important to reassure the citizens of Velhan's Claim, <name>, that they'll get through this. Hope is everything in dark times.

passages.title: Situational Awareness
passages.text:
We're here to help. But I've learned in the past, that there are times hope and reassurance can be the most urgent need.

While you were talking with the residents, Taenar and I have determined what our next steps are going to be. 

We need to give the people room to breathe, but we also need to prepare them to fight.

passages.title: The One That Got Away
passages.text:
adventurer, my son is out with the kobyss. He convinced the other kids they should sneak out with him to fight. Said they should, "be brave like my dad". 

When they met a kobyss, the others all ran back here, while he ran toward the crashed ship, to lead it away.

I have not handled myself bravely, adventurer. The story of the Indomitable says I was a hero; those lies were my report. 

If there was ever a time to step up, it's now. But I'm no match for the kobyss alone. Come with me, adventurer--help me save Maximillian.

passages.title: The One That Got Away
passages.text: Stay focused, <name>--we have to find my son.

passages.title: The One That Got Away
passages.text:
I know it sounds trite, <name>, but I could never thank you enough for getting Max home safely.

Through all this, you've also shown me I need to be out front, leading the way for my people. I've seen there are outcomes worse than death. 

I can't undo the mistakes I've made in the past, but I can be certain not to repeat the pattern.

passages.title: Teach a Man to Fish
passages.text:
adventurer, the people of Velhan's Claim have been locked up inside, afraid of the dark, for too long. 

And there's plenty to fear out there, but these are capable, strong people. They should be driving the kobyss away, not hiding behind their walls. 

Get these spears to the people of Velhan's Claim. They've learned to hide from their problems, but we'll give them the means to take their lives back!

passages.title: Teach a Man to Fish
passages.text: Have you handed out those spears yet? The people need them to remind them what they're capable of.

passages.title: Teach a Man to Fish
passages.text:
I think now we'll see them acting very differently, now that they're armed, <name>.

There's something about knowing you can take care of yourself, that you can handle your own problems, and you don't need anyone to rescue you.

Of course, we Lamplighters will always be there to help, but it's very likely that we won't be needed next time.

passages.title: Reclaiming Velhan's Claim
passages.text:
The problem I see, adventurer, is the kobyss. There's just so many of them.

Everyone here was serving in the Empire's military when we arrived in Hallowfall. They may be rusty now, but they've all trained before, and know how to be dangerous.

But we need to eliminate every disadvantage, including the kobyss numbers. So head out there and even up the numbers. Aemyra and I will keep everyone safe here.

passages.title: Reclaiming Velhan's Claim
passages.text: How's it going out there, <name>? You sending those creatures of darkness back to the deeps?

passages.title: Reclaiming Velhan's Claim
passages.text:
You know, I've hated the kobyss ever since they were dragging my fellow stalwarts into the night as dinner guests.

Hopefully because of the work you've done, that won't happen to any of the citizens of Velhan's Claim, <name>.

passages.title: Lamp Lit
passages.text:
The kobyss normally live deep underwater, adventurer. When Beledar is at its brightest, they don't bother us. Other sources of bright light will usually keep them away, but definitely weaken them.

As Lamplighters, we not only go into the dark to protect those in need, but we provide them the light that will keep them safe. Go set up these torches along the perimeter, then meet us up at the dawntower behind Velhan's Claim.

passages.title: Lamp Lit
passages.text: Did you get those torches set, <name>? The people will be able to quickly light them whenever Beledar fades.

passages.title: Lamp Lit
passages.text:
You saved my son, <name>. You broke the spine of the attack on our home, gave us what we need to fight. 

You helped me to be the leader I'd pretended I was. Thank you.

The Lamplighters will always have allies in Velhan's Claim.

passages.title: We Don't Go to Taelloch
passages.text:
This troubled Machine Speaker was here to do something. But what? It looks like something really did some damage to him.

We shouldn't dally. 

We need to head into Taelloch and look for the foreman. Can you clear the entryway into the town? Someone could get hurt!

passages.title: We Don't Go to Taelloch
passages.text: There's not much to see in the foreman's office. If we want answers, we'll need to search the town.

passages.title: Ghost of a Company Town
passages.text:
The foreman isn't here. Obviously. But the evidence points to her being here recently. So perhaps she's still nearby!

We should go further into town and see if anyone has any idea where she might be.

Or maybe someone else can give us the answers we need. Maybe we'll find out on our own! Maybe it was some sort of attack or some kind of... sorry. I'm getting ahead of myself. Let's go investigate!

passages.title: Ghost of a Company Town
passages.text: Well... there's one question answered perhaps. Only to unearth a dozen more.

passages.title: Controlled Demolition
passages.text:
I know we've fought skardyn before, champion, but this... this is worse. 

I knew that skardyn were turning earthen into more skardyn, but I didn't expect... the crystals... the spikes... the roiling blue energy... that smell! Anyway, not what I expected at all. 

If we must venture out there, I'm taking down some of those abominations along the way.

passages.title: Controlled Demolition
passages.text: There's more to be done. We can't let this corruption spread.

passages.title: Controlled Demolition
passages.text: Maybe we've only killed a few skardyn from a much larger swarm. But we have to start somewhere.

passages.title: The High Speaker's Secret
passages.text:
We got what we came for. We need to return to Gundargaz. Brinthe has to know what happened here.

We'll go on ahead, adventurer. Meet us in Gundargaz.

passages.title: The High Speaker's Secret
passages.text:
Thank you for looking into the mystery plaguing Taelloch.

What did you find?

passages.title: A Poor Reception
passages.text:
There's strong evidence that the Radiant Song is a warning from Azeroth herself. A cry for help.

That's why we're here. If this vision truly is Azeroth's message, Magni will know what she's trying to tell us.

He should be in the Chamber of the Heart. Let's go.

passages.title: A Poor Reception
passages.text:
I know why you're here. It's the visions. Azeroth's voice, heard all across the lands. Ye thought I would know what she's trying to tell us. 

Well, ye thought wrong.

passages.title: Azeroth's Voice
passages.text:
I haven't spoken with Azeroth for years. At first I just didn't feel the need. Then I realized I had started to resent her. For leaving me like... this. And now I'm not sure if I can.

But I know the stakes. This Radiant Song of hers foretells something dire. And we need to know what.

First, we need to prepare the Heart Chamber. Can ye start up the consoles nearby?

passages.title: Azeroth's Voice
passages.text: I understand Magni's concerns, but we have no other choice. The future of our world is at stake. We must try everything we can to understand what Azeroth is trying to warn us of.

passages.title: Azeroth's Voice
passages.text: This has never happened before. Magni is the Speaker of Azeroth. Why would communing with her cause him to collapse?

passages.title: Painful Lessons
passages.text:
Magni appears stable for now, but he's still not responsive. We need to get him treatment quickly. I'll open a portal to Dalaran.

Follow us when you can.

passages.title: Painful Lessons
passages.text:
I'm unsure why the Speaker of Azeroth would end up in such a state after attempting to... well, speak with Azeroth.

All we can do is wait for Magni to recover.

passages.title: A Mysterious Warning
passages.text:
Well, that was quite the nap. I wasn't expecting Azeroth to be so... loud. To normal folk, she's gently calling out. But with our connection, it felt like she was screaming. Directly into my crystal noggin.

I saw it though. Khaz Algar, an island of earthen, bathed in fire and smoke. That's where Azeroth is trying to lead us.

That's what we need to protect.

passages.title: A Mysterious Warning
passages.text: Khaz Algar...

passages.title: A Mysterious Warning
passages.text:
The council has decided. We travel to Khaz Algar.

Dalaran will teleport as soon as we're able. Will you lend us your aid in our preparations?

passages.title: Strengthen the Wards
passages.text:
Magni's vision foretells that Khaz Algar may be enduring some... turbulent times. And so it is best to ensure that Dalaran is ready for the worst.

Here, take this wand. It's been attuned with Dalaran's defense magics.

Just wave it near strategic parts of the city to strengthen our magical defenses.

passages.title: Strengthen the Wards
passages.text: We will be hard pressed to save Khaz Algar if our own defenses aren't strong enough to withstand attack.

passages.title: Strengthen the Wards
passages.text:
Well done, champion.

Let's just hope it's enough. I would hate for anything to happen to our city right as the world needs us most.

passages.title: Citizens of Dalaran
passages.text:
Our citizens must be prepared for Dalaran's departure. Can you ask around the city and see if anyone requires aid?

I'd also like for you to speak with Brann and Archmage Drenden. They both had concerns that would be best to address before we depart for Khaz Algar.

passages.title: Citizens of Dalaran
passages.text: Dalaran is always ready to defend the world, but that doesn't mean we can do so on a whim. Preparations are key to a smooth transportation.

passages.title: Citizens of Dalaran
passages.text: Thank you for your help. It's important that the citizens of Dalaran are ready for whatever may come.

passages.title: To Khaz Algar!
passages.text:
From what Magni has seen, Khaz Algar may not be the safest of destinations. We'll be relying on your aid, should a fight break out.

Let me know when you're ready to depart.

passages.title: To Khaz Algar!
passages.text:
She was Archmage Drenden. All along, Xal'atath has been watching, plotting, right in front of me. How could I be so blind? 

And now she's invading Dalaran with an army of nerubians. 

Xal'atath planned this. All of this. She wanted us to come to Khaz Algar.

passages.title: Before I Depart
passages.text:
I can feel my energy reserves depleting.

I will soon not be able to execute my duties. That is why I have Urtago here to take over.

Before my systems grind to a halt, I must make sure Mourning Rise is free of kobolds. They have invaded the memorial site I tend and plunder the Unbound shrines and bodies that are there.

Maybe it is good you are here. You may have the strength to help us.

Please, help Urtago rid the site of kobolds.

passages.title: Before I Depart
passages.text:
Korgran still calls himself the caretaker, but I'm the one who has been taking care of Mourning Rise for some time.

I don't mind. Korgran is very kind. 

But the situation here has gotten away from me. We have some work ahead of us.

passages.title: Who Runs This Fine Establishment?
passages.text:
While you were dealing with the tunnels and the workmasters, I saw a peculiar kobold go into a cave to the northwest. The kobolds seemed to respect him more than the others, calling him Grand-Heister Bokk and offering him the food you call "cheese." This makes me think he is the real mastermind.

If that kobold is in fact the real Ward of this operation, then we should take the opportunity to strike him down.

I will meet you at this cave.

passages.title: Who Runs This Fine Establishment?
passages.text:
I am happy to see you, <name>.

I feel my inner workings grinding--that's a sign of anxiety. Korgran nears his shutdown with every passing moment, and then this place will be under my care. 

It is a lot of responsibility. But I believe that I am ready for it.

passages.title: Lost Delivery
passages.text:
<You find a small yet heavy leather-bound package on the road with an attached label.>

Gundargaz Courier Express

EXPEDITED

To: 
Harvester Farnee
Durgaz Cabin

OPEN WITH CARE: Contains volatile elemental minerals.

passages.title: Lost Delivery
passages.text:
Well, smoke the hive... you found it! I still can't believe the courier just lost my package...

We've been waiting on this to help with Shalehoof's leg. 

Mixed with fire honey, this stuff should patch him up quickly!

passages.title: A Shadow Over Gundargaz
passages.text:
You look dangerous.

<Toki spits on the ground.>

That's good. We need dangerous. Something is stalking Gundargaz. 

Something mean. 

Something... recent. 

Just before the Coreway collapsed I started getting reports of workers going missing mid-shift. Only thing we've been able to find have been the odd chunk of rock.

Fingers, mostly. 

If you could sniff out what's stalking my town, I'd be in your debt.

passages.title: A Shadow Over Gundargaz
passages.text: Life didn't always used to be this exciting.

passages.title: A Shadow Over Gundargaz
passages.text:
A demon? Escaped from the crashed ruins of a flying magical city?

If you say so. 

I'm just glad it's sorted.

passages.title: Heeeelllp!!!
passages.text:
Hey! You!

Get me down! Away from these worms! Please!

I'll pay you! I'll even owe you one! Heck, I'll gladly sell out any cartel member you need dirt on! 

Just get me down!

Also, don't walk too much. They can hear your footsteps. Move from rock to rock if you don't want a swarm coming after you.

passages.title: Heeeelllp!!!
passages.text: Okay, okay! I'm okay.

passages.title: Delegated Dig
passages.text:
Okay, I know when I'm beat. So I want to hire you as my Champion of Coin... or coinchamp.

This is all a part of my brilliant enterprising venture. See, these worms here are great at rooting out rich minerals like a niffen sniffing out high-quality mushrooms. 

I'm willing to bet all of my money--and your life--that they found a vein of sivstone. Great stuff, though I doubt a <class> would know how to use it. 

Tell you what, you bring me a shipment's worth and I'll go halfsies on the profits with ya!

passages.title: Delegated Dig
passages.text: You get the goods?

passages.title: Delegated Dig
passages.text:
Nice haul! This should get us started back in Mmarl and show those goons who's who. 

Here's your cut.

passages.title: Squashing the Threat
passages.text:
I need your help!

The massive Shadow-Soured squash have begun to grow all over the place. They're stinky and crawling with nasty mites.

Mom and Dad brought in some airships to help us yank them out, but it's risky business with all those bugs.

Can you attach ropes to these Shadow-Soured Squash, and the airships can then haul them away without making a mess?

passages.title: Squashing the Threat
passages.text: Have you removed all the Squash?

passages.title: Squashing the Threat
passages.text: You did it! I heard stories of one time the squash was so heavy the airship crashed! Glad that didn't happen.

passages.title: Tricks of the Dark
passages.text:
Kobyss lurk in the shallows of murky water and snatch any who come near, faster than a viper!

And that's just when they hunt alone. In numbers, they are a swarm to be reckoned with. They've been a plague on our outskirt villages since the day we arrived. 

They eat victims alive, given the chance. We must rescue the villagers that have already been dragged to the water!

passages.title: Tricks of the Dark
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. These people are badly hurt, but I think they will make it. Some seem to have some skill in healing of their own.

passages.title: The Sweet Eclipse
passages.text:
I've set out to create a dessert that transcends the ordinary, one that even the most devout followers of the light would savor!

To balance the flavors of the desert, between light and shadow, I require ingredients from several areas within the darkness.

Please assist me in harvesting the following ingredients: Frog-Kissed Caviar, Darkroot Persimmon and Ethereal Sugar.

passages.title: The Sweet Eclipse
passages.text: Have you found all of the ingredients?

passages.title: The Sweet Eclipse
passages.text: Now the magic happens. Please sample this creation for yourself.

passages.title: Blades of the Arathi
passages.text:
I trust in your strength. I must ask you to go ahead to reinforce Sina's Yearning. Anduin and I can see my people to safety in Lorel's Crossing.

With the darkness and the kobyss, the hearts of my people in Sina's Yearning will be faltering to fear. We can't let them wallow.

Light a torch with the Sacred Flame in the center of town and use it to inspire my people's valor. Remind them of their strength.

We will catch up with you. May the Flame guide you, my friend.

passages.title: Blades of the Arathi
passages.text: The Arathi are strong. Proud. The kobyss may be vile but they will not win this day.

passages.title: Shadow upon Shadow
passages.text:
<Faerin's wide eyes dart around in surprise.>

What just happened? Did you see that shadow? And the oil well... it's gone dark? 

I've never seen anything like this before. 

Could it be the nearby dawntower? Hurry!

passages.title: Shadow upon Shadow
passages.text: The fear and shame of these people lingers in the air like a fog.

passages.title: Cutting Off the Legs
passages.text:
While we've yet to locate Xal'atath, we've received reports from deeper in the field of certain nerubians giving orders. It won't buy us too much but every action is critical.

Take them out. Hopefully that will allow us some breathing room. 

Speak with Anduin after you are done. He and the Arathi girl went after Alleria.

passages.title: Cutting Off the Legs
passages.text: Speak with Anduin within the Sanguine Grasps.

passages.title: Cutting Off the Legs
passages.text: Oh, good, you made it.

passages.title: Harvest Havoc
passages.text:
Our parents went off to fight the monsters that invaded our farm. While they are gone, we try to keep the farm running. 

We have a harvestbot to help with chores, but I keep crashing it into the river. We could finish our chores if you could help us drive the harvestbot!

passages.title: Harvest Havoc
passages.text: Have you completed the chores?

passages.title: Harvest Havoc
passages.text: You were really good at controlling Remy.  Maybe you can come back and help next week as well!

passages.title: Weapons and Warriors
passages.text:
Gorloc raiders have been slaughtering these farmers and stealing their pearls. They seek our protection, but we may not be enough.

I know of others nearby who can help. Seek them out and request their aid. If they are hesitant, offer them the promise of pearls as payment.

We will also need to arm these farmers so they can defend themselves. Search for spare weapons and equipment that they might be able to use.

I will go with the farmers and train them as best I can.

passages.title: Weapons and Warriors
passages.text: Good work. I'm glad you were able to recruit some fighters. It is worse than I expected, and we will need every one we have.

passages.title: Frontline Farmers
passages.text:
Most of the farmers are already out in the field, defending their positions. I have trained them as best I could given the circumstances, but they are still wielding farming tools. 

I need you to distribute the weapons you gathered to those on the frontlines. While it may not markedly improve their combat ability, at least it will boost their confidence that they are not alone in this fight.

passages.title: Frontline Farmers
passages.text: Excellent. As long as they fight together and for each other, I believe we will be victorious.

passages.title: Consecrated Cleanup
passages.text:
Our Veneration Grounds have been desecrated. Its beauty marred. 

It's going to take a bigger effort, but I would appreciate anything you can do to cleanup our grounds.

passages.title: Consecrated Cleanup
passages.text: I wish you could have seen this place before the Kobyss arrived.

passages.title: Consecrated Cleanup
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. It may not have seemed like much, but this is one of our most sacred places. 

We remember our dead here. We... have a lot to remember.

passages.title: After the Storm
passages.text:
Turalyon and Geya'rah are training our new earthen allies as ground forces. But we will need more than that. We will need the Stormriders. 

Many were lost in the infiltration of the Stormperch and more to the nerubians. Their leader, Stormward Baelgrim, died valiantly.

The surviving Stormriders are being cared for at a triage station nearby. We need to do whatever is necessary to get them and their rooks back in the air. They will be the earthen's most potent weapon in the battles to come.

passages.title: After the Storm
passages.text:
I'm sorry about Shraubendre. She was just protecting me. And I lied to protect her.

But you truly don't intend to take her away? You just want to summon more stormrooks?

passages.title: Follow Miral
passages.text:
Tomothy's lynx, Miral, has been bugging me. I don't know what she wants but it is unusual to see her without my brother. She's a great farm cat, but she's still a cat, so maybe she's just bored with Tomothy today? I don't know. Maybe Tomothy got into some sort of trouble.

Can you find out what is bothering her for me?

passages.title: Follow Miral
passages.text: <Miral looks at you as if expecting something. You are being judged.>

passages.title: Follow Miral
passages.text: <Miral lets out a pleased sound and purrs at you.>

passages.title: Save Tomothy
passages.text: <Miral looks at you expectantly then looks at the ruins, then back to you, then to the ruins. You get the sense she wants you to go over there. Perhaps this is where Tomothy got lost?>

passages.title: Save Tomothy
passages.text: You saved my idiot brother from the darkness! Thank you.

passages.title: Expert Consultant
passages.text:
You alone are no longer sufficient. We require additional assistance, and the jawcrawlers and threadlings also need oversight.

The niffen settlement, Mmarl, is not far. However, past forced conscription attempts have failed. Nerubians are now forbidden within the settlement. We need someone to communicate in our stead.

Go and barter with the rats. Come back with able bodies.

passages.title: Expert Consultant
passages.text: The nerubians want our help again? I'd like to hear this...

passages.title: Bright Young Niffen
passages.text:
You need swarmhands, huh? 

Last time the nerubians wanted our help, they tried to force us. They're terrible negotiators! All we wanted was a little quid pro quo.

We've got several arachnologists, but most of them are busy keeping the flyers at bay. I'm sure they won't refuse an opportunity to study some swarmbeasts up close and personal! 

Maybe if you lighten their workload, they'll take you up on your offer.

passages.title: Bright Young Niffen
passages.text: Have you found anyone yet?

passages.title: Bright Young Niffen
passages.text: See? All we wanted was a little something in exchange.

passages.title: Rak-Ush Under New Management
passages.text:
Well, you got your swarmhands. 

What are you still doing here? Go on then, you don't need my permission!

Make sure the nerubians treat them fairly, now.

passages.title: Rak-Ush Under New Management
passages.text: Excellent.

passages.title: Beetle in a Haystack
passages.text:
There are still feral stagshells on the outskirts of Rak-Ush.

This scent grenade should be sufficient in stunning the beasts and alerting the niffen to their location.

Once they are stunned, one of the rats will take them back to their hollow.

Capture them and bring them back. We will be waiting.

passages.title: Beetle in a Haystack
passages.text: We still require more stagshells.

passages.title: Beetle in a Haystack
passages.text: Excellent work.

passages.title: Permanent Hire
passages.text:
Rak-Ush is beginning to look like a functioning swarmery.

The role of delegation has suited me and Vix'aron well. You will continue to aid the niffen. In return, you may keep a portion of the wealth the swarmbeasts produce. 

Saffrin has more detailed plans around the development of the swarmery. Go speak to him, I have nothing else to say to you.

passages.title: Permanent Hire
passages.text: You have not spoken to Saffrin yet, have you? Otherwise you would not be here.

passages.title: Permanent Hire
passages.text: These swarmbeasts aren't going to take care of themselves!

passages.title: Conduit of the Southern Storm
passages.text:
I'll tell you what I told Baelgrim when we last spoke. The binding of stormrooks is wrong. These creatures are as smart as any earthen. Some I'd say are smarter.

But... Lufsela seems to be different. If her stormrook follows her willingly, then perhaps others will make that choice as well if she summons them.

To summon rooks, we need Baelgrim's conduit. It's tucked away here somewhere. Have a look around, and maybe ask these pilgrims if they have seen it.

passages.title: Conduit of the Southern Storm
passages.text: Have you found the conduit?

passages.title: Conduit of the Southern Storm
passages.text:
Not only was Olbarig once a Stormrider, but he served as Baelgrim's right hand as a Stormguard for a long time. Seems they had a falling out over the rooks.

But Olbarig says that the conduit will serve as a beacon. If the stormrooks of Skywall are willing, it will guide them through the storm. He also seems to think I should be the one to use it.

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! Lord Andestrasz has left the Dragon Isles and is visiting Stormwind. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, skyrider!

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! Lord Andestrasz has left the Dragon Isles and is visiting Orgrimmar. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Outland Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, dragonrider!

passages.title: Rook Rally
passages.text:
Now that we've got the conduit all charged, I suppose it's time we joined everyone on the peak. 

Thrall talked me through what to expect, but also said summoning the stormrooks will require me to trust my feelings and instincts.

An earthen trusting their feelings and instincts. That's... a challenge.

You will help me, right? I'm not a fighter, and it looks dangerous up there. 

If anything happens to me, make sure Shraubendre makes it out safe. Please.

passages.title: Rook Rally
passages.text:
Well done. It seems the rooks of Skywall haven't just answered the call. 

They were reaching out to us, and they have chosen their own riders for this new generation. 

I am honored to have played a role in the ritual.

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! You just missed Lord Andestrasz. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, dragonrider!

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! Lord Andestrasz has left the Dragon Isles and is visiting Stormwind. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, dragonrider!

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Skyrider! Lord Andestrasz has left the Dragon Isles and is visiting Orgrimmar. He's looking for capable skyriders like yourself to compete in new races!

passages.title: The Northrend Cup Begins
passages.text: Thank you for visiting, dragonrider!

passages.title: Alone in the Dark
passages.text:
My people do not think that this Black Blood is a threat to our world. It has sat dormant for ages, after all. Why should that change now?

But the world is changing more quickly than my people realize. The nerubians' decision to extract the Blood for their own ends is proof of that.

The nerubians hold a watchtower not far from here. The ones who survived the pit could not have gotten too far. We should give chase immediately.

passages.title: Alone in the Dark
passages.text: <The spider looks at you expectantly.>

passages.title: Alone in the Dark
passages.text: <The bizarre creature's eyes remain locked upon you, unwavering. It nudges something towards you--a scroll with a thick seal of violet wax.>

passages.title: Goldbricking
passages.text:
Is this what we are to rely on to help us defeat Xal'atath? The Unbound define themselves by their desertion. And the Oathsworn, for being made of stone, are pretty soft. City life hasn't done them any favors. 

We've got a lot of work to do.

Get down there and give these earthen a taste of what it's like to face a real threat. Try not to knock any "offline," but a maiming here or there would send a strong message to the rest.

passages.title: Goldbricking
passages.text: Don't go easy on them. They're made of stone after all.

passages.title: Goldbricking
passages.text:
You lit a fire down there, and we will continue to fan the flames. 

Go now, secure in knowing you have helped set these earthen on the path to glory. The nerubians won't know what hit them!

passages.title: Metal and Stone
passages.text:
While some of these recruits struggle with discipline, most have a strong work ethic. They only need training and the equipment to make the most of it.

Earthen weaponsmiths and armorers have been working around the clock to equip this fledgling army. But we could use some help getting the new armaments into the hands of these trainees.

passages.title: Metal and Stone
passages.text: Check in with Vindicator Jaelaana. She is in charge of distributing the weapons though she can be rather stingy. Be sure she doesn't send too many off for hand-to-hand training.

passages.title: Metal and Stone
passages.text: Now they're starting to look like a real army. We'll continue with their training, but I believe you have more important matters to attend to.

passages.title: Ground Pounders
passages.text:
The rooks and their chosen riders will need time to bond. 

Perhaps you should use this time to check in on our other trainees. 

The Stormriders are the traditional army of the earthen, but many Unbound and Oathsworn have expressed willingness to fight at our side due to help in restoring their machines.

Adelgonn, Geya'rah, and Turalyon are busy training them. Go and see if they need any assistance.

passages.title: Ground Pounders
passages.text:
Someone save me from all this bickering. Alliance this, Horde that... 

I've never encountered anything like it in my thousands of years even amongst the Oathsworn and Unbound. If they committed half the energy they expend on posturing towards training, our task would be complete by now.

See what help you can offer my people. They need real mentorship if we are to be ready for the next nerubian offensive.

passages.title: Flight Training 101
passages.text:
Now that all of our recruits are present, it's high time we took to the air. See what I did there? High time? No?

Right then. We'll be puttin' these rookies through their paces. Startin' with the basics of aerial maneuverin' at speed, we'll do our best to simulate the kind of precision flyin' we might expect below ground. 

After that, we'll see what these rooks can really do--an I think Thrall and Lufsela have somethin' special cookin'.

passages.title: Flight Training 101
passages.text: Let's set a good example for these new riders. Lead them through the course as quick as ye can.

passages.title: Flight Training 101
passages.text:
There you have it! Raw recruits made of stone, soarin' on the backs of birds made of lightnin'. Proof that ol' Kurdran can teach anythin' to fly!

But we're not done yet.

passages.title: The Nibelgaz Refinery
passages.text:
Quickly! Elementals have overrun the Nibelgaz Mine and the refinery crew are trapped down there with them. 

I am especially worried about my fused, Munderut. His memory is not the best these days. If you are a friend, rescue him and the refinery workers.

Here, take this healing clay. It only helps a little, but it should be enough for any injured to make their way back. I wish we had a rejuvenating crystal, but that is the stuff of legends.

passages.title: The Nibelgaz Refinery
passages.text:
The workers told me that you helped them escape the refinery. Task complete! 

I'll take the clay back now. Gratitude.

passages.title: Rampage in the Refinery
passages.text:
Catastrophe! Oh, this is awful. Awful! Those accursed slag heap elementals are keeping my refinery workers from being able to do their jobs.

Duty demands we carry on our work. These delays will not be tolerated. You look competent enough. Go on, get down there and get to work destroying elementals. Production must not be slowed!

passages.title: Rampage in the Refinery
passages.text: Well? Did you destroy them? I need my crew back to work immediately!

passages.title: Rampage in the Refinery
passages.text:
What a terrible delay in production. The miners will have to work twice as hard to make up for lost time, I am afraid.

It is good you came around when you did. Those elementals are a menace. An awful menace!

passages.title: Gutting the Pool
passages.text:
The kobyss are... a bit larger than I expected, and I might--might, you understand?--have more trouble with them than I originally anticipated.

Kill any stupid fish-faces you see.

passages.title: Gutting the Pool
passages.text: Yes, make them bleed. Make them pay!

passages.title: Gutting the Pool
passages.text:
You've killed a lot of them.

I wouldn't mind if you killed more. Just saying.

passages.title: A Final Goodbye
passages.text:
Well, parents avenged, fish killed, more fish killed, biggest fish killed. 

Pretty good day.

I guess I should go burn stuff.

passages.title: A Final Goodbye
passages.text:
Thanks, <name>. I'll make sure to put in a good word with General Steelstrike for you. I know her well. 

Well, I met her once. 

Well, I saw her in the street.

But I did think about talking to her, so it's the same thing really.

passages.title: The Edicts
passages.text:
Merrix and Adelgonn will be expecting an update. On my way here, I heard that they're all heading to the Proscenium to commit to the war officially. You should go and brief them on the readiness of the Stormriders.

I'd like a moment with Zarein here. But we'll be along soon. And we'll be bringing Baelgrim's spirit with us.

passages.title: The Edicts
passages.text: This is a critical moment for all earthen.

passages.title: The Edicts
passages.text: Titans... what have they done?

passages.title: Seeds of Salvation
passages.text:
These once obedient harvestbots have run amok and are wreaking havoc in our fields.

The success of our community depends on getting our seeds in the ground, but most of the seeds are in the hands of those harvesters!

Would you venture into the fields, eliminate any rogue machines, gather the seeds, and finish the planting?

passages.title: Seeds of Salvation
passages.text: Have you planted the seeds?

passages.title: Seeds of Salvation
passages.text: You've truly done us a great service! Planting those seeds buys us valuable time until the harvestbots are repaired.

passages.title: Dereliction of Duty
passages.text:
A moment, if you have one.

One of my lieutenants, Shinda Creedpike, did not report in at first bonfire. That may not seem like a large issue to you, but the Arathi in Hallowfall survive only because we follow orders and stand for our brethren.

I am not cruel. I do not want to punish a man for his weakness in this terrible environment. Can you find him and bring him back? 

Take all the time you need.

passages.title: Dereliction of Duty
passages.text:
Dawnsurge must have sent you.

It seems like my respite is over.

passages.title: Dereliction of Duty
passages.text:
You're speaking my language, <name>. Plans give me structure and a goal to achieve.

Let me think about the optimal way to relax.

passages.title: Fishing is Good for the Soul
passages.text:
I used to fish with my mother at the local pond when I was a child. It wasn't the fish that made the experience--my mother was famously terrible at cooking--but the tranquility and bonding time.

Perhaps I could find a portion of that peace again here. There's a spot south of Mereldar that the others use to fish. I'll meet you there!

passages.title: Fishing is Good for the Soul
passages.text: Maybe I can find peace in the act of fishing.

passages.title: Fishing is Good for the Soul
passages.text:
I wish we could have fished. But if today confirmed anything to me, I have relearned a valuable truth.

If I lay down my sword, these children would have to pick them up if they are to survive this place. They have known no other place than this land.

They will see our homeland. They must see our homeland.

passages.title: Burnout
passages.text: Please return to Commander Dawnsurge and give them my sincere apologies for my absence. I will submit myself for punishment for my trespass after my shift.

passages.title: Burnout
passages.text:
I will not institute any punishment for his absence. I'm simply glad you were there to support him when I could not.

We are living in times of prophecy, <name>. It is a curse I would not bestow upon anyone. We must do what we must to survive these days.

passages.title: A Moment to Rest
passages.text:
Good, you're both here. 

I have a favor to ask. 

Faerin's wandered off. I think it might help if you and your... disheveled friend here find her. 

She'll be in Light's Redoubt.

passages.title: A Moment to Rest
passages.text: <Anduin chews his lip, lost in thought.>

passages.title: Supply the Effort
passages.text:
When shadow fell upon our town, many necessary supplies were taken in the cover of darkness.

With the light returning, it is time to rebuild, but first, we must retrieve what was lost. 

Search the surrounding areas, recover any supplies that might be useful.

passages.title: Supply the Effort
passages.text: Have you recovered the stolen items?

passages.title: Supply the Effort
passages.text: You have recovered far more than we could have hoped.  I've set some of the extras aside for you to have.

passages.title: Infested Infestation
passages.text:
These spore-afflicted beasts at Pillar-nest Vosh been a thorn in our side since setting up Faerin's Advance. They be spreading thick clouds of spores. I never be seeing anything like it!

They already attacked once. Won't be long till they attack again. If we got any hope of survivin', we need to cull dere numbers. 

Go to Pillar-nest Vosh and take some of those spore-afflicted beasts out!

passages.title: Infested Infestation
passages.text: With de number of those spore-afflicted beasts reduced, we bought more time ta think of a more permanent solution.

passages.title: Spinning Spore Spines
passages.text:
Orsenth sent you? And we are supposedly fused? Why... so I am wearing a medallion. But I have no memory... Well, no time for that.

Did you see the spinning spores on your way here? I need the spines that they grow for... I need them for... now what was it again? Oh yes! There is no better instrument for carving out the fine detail that my work as a gem carver requires than those spines. Will you collect some?

I will make my way back to the refinery. I am eager to get back and meet this Orsenth.

passages.title: Spinning Spore Spines
passages.text:
Why, what is this now? You're a stranger to these depths, are you not? What are you doing here?

<You remind him of all you've spoken of.>

Well, what are you waiting for? Go and get me those spines!

passages.title: Spinning Spore Spines
passages.text:
Where did you come from? Who are you?

I do not know how you knew I needed these spines, but I thank you. There is no better instrument for carving out the fine detail that my work as a gem carver requires. I am a gem carver, you see!

Have you met my new friend Orsenth? What- what was I saying?

passages.title: To the Source
passages.text:
Orsenth told me you have been instrumental in dealing with the elemental problem here at the mine. I am Keldaz, supervisor for the militia. We came as soon as word of the attack reached us in Gundargaz. The miners you rescued said that the elementals poured out of the northeast mine shaft. 

I will leave some of my guards here to lend their support and have sent for reinforcements. If you are still willing to help, meet me outside the cave and let us see what we can do to staunch the flow of elementals.

passages.title: To the Source
passages.text: Ah, <name>, you made it. We did as well, but were attacked often on our way over. Unfortunately, Nanthaz took a heavy blow and needs time to recover.

passages.title: Broken Memories
passages.text: Something about this particular gemstone feels important. Perhaps it would be worthwhile to bring it to Speaker Brinthe.

passages.title: Broken Memories
passages.text:
Earthen use these gems to hold memories we would otherwise lose to the unrelenting march of time.

When an earthen goes into stasis, we sometimes use a memory gem to witness their final moments.

During our lives, we use them to carry our precious memories to the Archive, where they can be stored. Then we recharge our bodies and renew our minds in the Awakening Machine.

Thank you for returning this, <name>. Even shattered and faded, it's still precious.

passages.title: Web of Manipulation
passages.text:
This town has been under siege, overrun by spiders! Even when we clear them out, they always return.

Something is behind these attacks!

A small ledge northeast of Light's Bloom harbors these spiders. Scout out the ledge. Find out what is driving these spiders to attack us, and put an end to it!

passages.title: Web of Manipulation
passages.text: Have you solved our spider problem?

passages.title: Web of Manipulation
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  Now let us see if that puts an end to this eight-legged invasion!

passages.title: Back to Base
passages.text:
Getting this factory up and running will be a challenge, but I think we'll figure out something. Let's head back to Gundargaz and consult with a friend of ours.

His mind will be a big help to us here.

passages.title: Back to Base
passages.text: Are you ready to put our heads together and come up with a plan?

passages.title: The Unusual Bug
passages.text: Nerubians in Rak-Ush may find this strange little spider of interest.

passages.title: The Unusual Bug
passages.text: Oh, I was wondering where those had gone, thank you for returning it!

passages.title: The Lost Flame
passages.text:
<A tinderbox of a Hallowfall Expedition member, its return would help honor the memory of those who bravely gave their lives.>

An expedition scout might possess knowledge about this item.>

passages.title: The Lost Flame
passages.text:
On the Day of Shadows, Augustine panicked and broke ranks.

There were rumors he had left Hallowfall and found a way to the surface. I see he failed.

passages.title: A Small Bag of Seeds
passages.text: <This small bag of seeds seems forgotten, perhaps Aliya Hillhelm could make use of them.>

passages.title: A Small Bag of Seeds
passages.text: Why thank you!

passages.title: Mineral Water Woes
passages.text:
When that magic hammer fell into the Deeps, I knew it could be a formidable weapon against the skardyn menace. Your friend has told me that it's 'particular' about its wielder.

Fortunately, I am a hero!

And as a hero, I know how to get close to it. We need to have a good mix of pollen and water plastered onto us. That way, the beast standing over it will think we're just like it.

That mineral water has to be the exact right temperature to mix with the lashroom dust and blend in.

passages.title: Mineral Water Woes
passages.text:
That was a right pain. But we got the water Berrund asked for.

It's time we get a move on. I don't want my father's hammer to just languish there in the mud. That doesn't sit right with me, not at all.

passages.title: Put On a Good Face
passages.text:
Berrund here says that the massive beast standing over Fearbreaker is very particular about what kinds of creatures it allows near it.

If we blend in, he says, we can get close enough tae nab the hammer. But tae blend in, he says we have tae get covered by the dust an' pollen in the grotto. 

Those Lashrooms look like they're a good place to start. 

It all seems suspicious tae me, but fer now, we'll play along until I can recover Fearbreaker and bring it back to my father.

passages.title: Put On a Good Face
passages.text: Have you gathered up that dust? It's the only way you're going to get near that hammer, especially with that creature wandering around.

passages.title: Put On a Good Face
passages.text:
<Berrund the Gleaming appears not to have a speck of pollen on himself.>

You got yourself good and covered in that lashroom dust, all right.

I'm a bit surprised you're not itching and sneezing, like your friend here.

passages.title: Epicenter
passages.text:
There is the creature standing between us and that magic hammer. It certainly made an impact when it landed here in the Ringing Deeps, didn't it? Look at the size of that crater!

With the pollen and water splashed on you like this, you should be able to approach that beast and, theoretically, not be harmed. You'll blend right in with it!

But if it does turn aggressive, don't worry, I'll be right behind you.

We'll get that hammer out of here safely!

passages.title: Epicenter
passages.text:
Why that amber-sucking, slime-spined, travesty of an earthen! I've met troggs with more honor!

He took Fearbreaker! He took my family's hammer and left us to die to that creature!

This cannot stand. I will not allow such disrespect to you... or to me.

passages.title: Boiling Mad
passages.text:
That gravel-brained ingrate! He took Fearbreaker and ran off to the north!

It's not that I want that hammer for myself. I don't. But it belongs to the Bronzebeard clan. It should be in the hands of someone who respects its power!

We need to track him down before he hurts himself or someone else with that hammer!

passages.title: Boiling Mad
passages.text:
These earthen have had a bad time of it.

Berrund's already run headlong into there, but if he was hoping to clean up the ills of the place, he's clearly in over his rocky head.

<Moira points to the nearby rocky contusion>

Look, he can barely keep hold o' Fearbreaker! What if he drops it and is killed? We need tae find him.

passages.title: Clean Up House
passages.text:
It looks like the destruction around the Coreway rattled loose more than just a few stones down here. It's stirred up all sorts o' dark things.

If this was a thriving mining operation, it ain't anymore. 

We need to help the earthen get it under control again, and that means thinning out these beasts.

passages.title: Clean Up House
passages.text: I want to get Fearbreaker back, but we need to clear out some of these agitated beasts first.

passages.title: Clean Up House
passages.text:
That's a mite better. At least there won't be so many of those creatures running amok around this area.

Now we've got other problems.

We've got skardyn.

passages.title: Fault Lines
passages.text:
Berrund took Fearbreaker for himself. I suppose he thought he could save these people. Be the hero.

But ye can't go about doing the wrong thing for the right reasons. I know from experience. If a rock is hollow tae begin with, it never can be solid again, no matter how hard ye try. 

He's likely tae need saving himself now. Let's find him in this blasted place.

passages.title: Fault Lines
passages.text: You found me?

passages.title: Fault Lines
passages.text:
<Berrund the Gleaming's skin is chipped and damaged. His eyes can barely focus. He is near to death.>

Every time... I tried to use the hammer... it just got away from me. I could have saved people. I don't... I don't...

passages.title: These Strong Hands
passages.text:
<Berrund the Gleaming coughs dustily.>

I knew I couldn't take the skardyn without some help. I thought, if I just had that magic hammer, then nothing would stop me. I had to have it, you see, or else, maybe I wasn't who I was made to be.

But it kept slipping out of my fingers. Like it didn't want anything to do with me. It fell out of my hands at the worst moment and now... <He coughs again.>
