It's clearly not mine. It never was. I'm... I'm... sorry.

passages.title: These Strong Hands
passages.text:
I thought this day would never come because my Da' would never have given me Fearbreaker. He probably would have wanted it to happen a different way.

But I have it now, and I'll make sure it gets back to him safe.

First though, we have unfinished business here.

passages.title: Fearbreaker
passages.text:
The skardyn have taken over the operations here in the Rumbling Wastes. That's why Berrund thought he needed Fearbreaker.

We're going to finish that job before I take the hammer back to Magni.

What kind of a queen would I be if I wasn't willing tae put myself in danger for the good of others? Let's get in there and save as many as we can.

passages.title: Fearbreaker
passages.text:
We got there in a roundabout way, but we still made a difference in the lives of these earthen.

Berrund, hopefully, has learned a lesson in real heroism. But I suppose we'll see in time.

Now, let's get this over with.

passages.title: The Bronzebeard Legacy
passages.text:
Well, we did what we set out tae do... and more. We found Fearbreaker and did some good with it.

Now it's time tae bring it back tae Magni.

Let's hope Berrund learned a lesson here, but I suspect he'll manage tae get himself in trouble again soon. Hopefully, it'll be fer the right reasons an' with the right support.

passages.title: The Bronzebeard Legacy
passages.text:
It's funny. I can see why me Da' was so fond o' this hammer. And what it meant when he trusted others tae hold onto it.

Fearbreaker's got a mind of its own, in ways. It wants what it wants. 

I suppose I relate.

passages.title: The Notebook
passages.text:
adventurer, I need your help. My whole future is on the line! I came to Lightspark to be an airship captain, and I've put in a ton of work to excel here. But my notebook is missing, with my final report!

I'm top in the class, but if I don't turn it in soon, I won't be our next airship captain. Please help me find it.

I thought I left it out by the canyon where we review each other's skiff piloting, but it wasn't there when I checked. Can you help me look for it?

passages.title: The Notebook
passages.text:
Edwyn took it? Of course. 

He desperately wants to be selected as captain, but he knows I'm ahead in the rankings. His only chance is if I can't turn in my report. We have to get it back!

passages.title: Height Club
passages.text:
I'm so tired of Edwyn. From the day we all arrived, he's been telling everyone he'll be selected as captain.

He's a great flyer--very talented, and he knows his stuff. But his ego gets in the way of treating people as he should. And he knows my grades and flight review scores are higher.

But if I can't turn in my report, he'll be the next captain. Take it back from him!

passages.title: Height Club
passages.text: Did you get it back? I'd love to see the look on Edwyn's face...

passages.title: Height Club
passages.text: He threw it into the valley and the WIND TOOK IT?!

passages.title: Gone with the Wind
passages.text:
I can't believe Edwyn threw my report out into the wind. 

Can you please track down what papers you can find? I'll look for any around the school grounds, you check the valley. 

This report is already late... But I had some really good insights around airship capabilities. When Headmaster Fynch sees them, maybe he'll still allow me to turn it in.

Bring me whatever pages you find!

passages.title: Gone with the Wind
passages.text: I hope you found all the pages, <name>!

passages.title: Gone with the Wind
passages.text:
I really wish this looked better. I'm honestly ashamed to turn it in, if Headmaster Fynch will even let me. 

But we have to try--the ideas are what matters, and they're still true!

passages.title: A Principled Principal
passages.text:
Great work gathering these up. I found a few blowing around up here, so I think we've got all the pages. Let's get this to Headmaster Fynch! He's probably in the classroom.

I sure hope he accepts it. He says he doesn't accept late work, but there were a lot of extenuating circumstances at play here. And if he doesn't, I'll be reporting to Edwyn as my captain. I'm not sure I could do that, after what's happened.

passages.title: A Principled Principal
passages.text:
Sophietta has been a phenomenal student. Honestly, I am too close to the situation to make that decision without bias. But it was too nuanced to reject without consideration.

As an outsider, I know your decision wasn't colored by months spent with these students, so I could trust your judgment. I appreciate your help in resolving the situation, <name>.

passages.title: Care Package
passages.text:
My cousin Sophietta and I came to Hallowfall together as stalwarts. Since arriving, we both lived here in Dunelle's Kindness for years. But she left last year to follow her dream of being one of our airship captains, or at least joining an airship crew.

She's a strong person, but I don't know how she's doing. Especially without Innkeeper Valrin's sweetrolls! She can't get them at Lightspark, the Sky Academy. Will you take these to her, and make sure she's doing alright?

passages.title: Care Package
passages.text: What's this? Are these for me?

passages.title: Care Package
passages.text: That was very kind of Barahl to send these. You can tell him I'm doing well, but first, do you think you could help me with something?

passages.title: Status Report
passages.text:
Airships give the Arathi Army command of the skies. But roads are the lifeblood of empires. My scouts protect and light the passageways of Hallowfall for our citizens.

One such patrol has been late to report their walk of the eastern road. Seek my missing scouts by the sight of smoke or flame. Arathi soldiers know better than to linger in the dark.

passages.title: Status Report
passages.text: <Scout Wayshelm does not meet your gaze.>

passages.title: Seek the Lost
passages.text:
Guard our ways, repel the dark. Civilize this twisted land. All in the name of our empire. This is the mission of the Arathi Army. A mission I can heed no longer.

I am afraid.

I won't go back into the dark. Not after what I've seen. If Maevest or any of my other companions survived, they must crave the mercy of a swift death. And I left them to that terror.

Tell Captain Trueflame her scouts died in darkness, one and all.

passages.title: Seek the Lost
passages.text: <Scout Wayshelm gazes into the flames of his campfire.>

passages.title: Seek the Lost
passages.text: <Scout Wayshelm clutches the compass tight and finally raises his gaze to regard you.>

passages.title: Stem the Flow
passages.text:
The roads were meant to be lit. But the path was overgrown, the lanterns dark. Swarming, frothing, and reeking with rot. It all happened so fast. By the time we realized the danger, the beasts were upon us. The largest of them was huge and black as night.

It is our duty to slay monsters and push back the darkness. But the thought of going back fills with me fear. 

I've lost my nerve. But you, outsider, can still make this right.

passages.title: Stem the Flow
passages.text: <Scout Maevest's compass gleams in the firelight. Wayshelm has bound it with twine and now wears it around his neck.>

passages.title: Stem the Flow
passages.text: You're alive. Praise the Sacred Flame.

passages.title: Mow the Masses
passages.text:
Maevest and I broke away from the others and fled, their screams left in our wake. Foul muck smothered our lanterns and we stumbled in the dark through knee-high waters. I heard a splash like she had tripped and fallen in, but I couldn't bring myself to look back.

Only later did I find the tiny bite marks on my ankles. Be warned, there's something in the water.

I took notice of fronds growing from the pools. Swarming insects feast on their sickly nectar. Destroy those plants and starve the beasts.

passages.title: Mow the Masses
passages.text:
<Scout Wayshelm gives you an approving nod and finds a grim smile.>

In the dark, even the plants want us dead.

passages.title: What Grows in the Dark
passages.text:
We are told never to walk in the darkness. To carry light wherever we go. The thought of returning this way filled me with dread. 

But your courage shines with splendor, <name>. At your side, my way is lit.

No more hiding. The beast clad in black chitin, the one that killed my friends, dies in that cave. I am with you.

passages.title: What Grows in the Dark
passages.text:
Wayshelm told me everything.

A debt of gratitude is owed. To you, and to the scouts who gave their life for our empire.

passages.title: The Glittering Shard
passages.text:
<Glistening with an inner light, this shard of crystal feels warm to the touch..

Orsenth may be interested in examining this piece of ore.>

passages.title: The Glittering Shard
passages.text:
A crystal shard? From a glittering cave? Why does that sound familiar to me?

<She takes the crystal in her hands to examines more closely.>

This can't be! It's the healing crystal I mentioned earlier! We thought it was lost. What a wonder to hold it in my hands...

<She sighs deeply, looking at Munderut.>

I wish it could mend our minds as well as it mends our wounds. We need to get the vault back up and running.

passages.title: The Fleet Arrives
passages.text:
From the moment we crashed on this isle, it were clear as crystal we'd be needin' allies if we hoped to face Xal'atath. 

Jaina and Thrall took off tae muster reinforcements, an' you and I set tae work seein' what could be done here with the earthen.

An' I have to say we've done well on our own, haven't we? 

<Moira smiles at you proudly.>

But it looks like our reinforcements may have finally arrived. Peacekeepers spied ships comin' this way. Go take a look an' confirm the good news!

passages.title: The Fleet Arrives
passages.text:
I'm glad to see you are well, <name>.

The journey took longer than anticipated. The capricious sea had its own plans it seems.

passages.title: The Last Journey
passages.text:
This lantern is perfect.

Enough of this. It is time! I can feel my memory clouding. We have to get going. Urtago is waiting for us. They will join us on my final journey to Mourning Rise, where we will conduct a ceremony.

<Korgran forces a smile.>

It is nothing fancy, I promise. As I said, it is more symbolic than anything else.

My head feels heavy. What was I doing again? Hmm, oh, right! Meeting Urtago!

passages.title: The Last Journey
passages.text:
<name>, we have to find Korgran! If he keeps on exerting himself, he will shutdown in the middle of nowhere.

And it's not safe for him to be out in his condition. He would be easy prey for stormfangs and even kobolds.

passages.title: A Change of Tradition
passages.text:
An Unbound earthen can't return to the Coreway, so we have Mourning Rise. But looking at Korgran, remembering our last conversation before...

I may not be the Mourning Rise caretaker just yet, but with Korgran's condition, it falls to me to be in charge. 

As Unbound, we made our own rules and traditions. So what if he doesn't want to stand at Mourning Rise? If a seaside memorial is what Caretaker Korgran wants, that's what he gets.

<name>, meet me at the shore to the southeast of here.

passages.title: A Change of Tradition
passages.text:
He enjoyed the walk, but it has taken a heavy toll on him.

Korgran barely recognizes me now.

passages.title: Everyday I'm Snufflin'
passages.text: Perhaps the kobolds of Gundargaz would be interested in this Odd Glob of Wax.

passages.title: Everyday I'm Snufflin'
passages.text: You snuffle something good?

passages.title: Everyday I'm Snufflin'
passages.text:
Middles always need more wax for project.

Trade bigger, shinier ruby for if have lots. Get fancier things for helping.

Keep snufflin'. Keep trading.

passages.title: Urban Odyssey
passages.text:
Did ye hear, <name>?

A lot of folks from the city are eager to lend a hand an' support our attack on the nerubians and Xal'atath. I think it's worth reachin' out tae them tae see how they could pitch in.

The more support we gather, the better.

passages.title: Urban Odyssey
passages.text: I am glad to see you return, <name>.

passages.title: Urban Odyssey
passages.text:
Thank ye, <name>. The more people we get on board with helpin', the more successful we'll be.

But we won't get anywhere if we dunnae have a large enough fightin' force.

The earthen are nae in good shape. But I think Alleria may be helpin' with that.

passages.title: Chew On That
passages.text:
Fishing out here is not easy, especially when the spooky sounds of the darkness start to wear on the nerves.

I've taken to chewing on the Duskstem from the tall plants nearby. It's sweet and chewy, keeps the jaw busy, and helps me pass the time!

If you could lend a hand by gathering some Duskstem with your flying mount, I would be most appreciative.

passages.title: Chew On That
passages.text: Have you collected enough?

passages.title: Chew On That
passages.text: You made that look easy. It usually takes me an hour to climb one of those plants.

passages.title: Entrepreneur, Inc.
passages.text:
Okay, color me impressed. You are officially my Coinchamp! It's like a champion, only I pay you to do things. A mercenary, only with better branding.

You should meet my business partner, Ripsnoodle. He's working out some deals with his own coinchamps with the niffin over at Mmarl. He might have more work for you--though I recommend not buying anything he tries to sell you.

You can find Mmarl east of here. Just follow your nose, you can smell it from a mile away.

passages.title: Entrepreneur, Inc.
passages.text: Skedgit actually found something out there? She always did have a good nose for business.

passages.title: The Machine Speakers
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer! The <race> of the hour... We were just discussing you.

<Moira nods towards Speaker Brinthe.>

There is some unfinished business for us to attend to, now that the High Speaker's transgressions have been corrected and the Awakening Machine restored once more.

Care to stick around?

passages.title: The Machine Speakers
passages.text: It is a new day in the Ringing Deeps.

passages.title: Prisoner Preservation
passages.text:
The beasts took our people! Dragged them away when we were gettin' our first rest since our escape!

We only just escaped those nerubians. We can't afford ta lose more people.

Search Pillar-nest Vosh. It's where all those beasts came from. If we're lucky our people are still alive.

passages.title: Prisoner Preservation
passages.text: Survivin' ain't easy, but we gotta keep pushin' on.

passages.title: Prisoner Preservation
passages.text: You did all you could. I be in your debt. We be honorin' Jeti's memory by dealing with da nest.

passages.title: Antifungal Firestarter
passages.text:
Consider it a professional hunch, but those spores comin' out of those fungal pods and the ones afflictin' all da beasts are connected. 

Maybe if we destroy da fungal spore pods it'll slow whatever control those fungarians have on da beasts.

Take these antifungal firebombs and torch as many fungal spore pods as you can!

passages.title: Antifungal Firestarter
passages.text: Too many strange tings occur this far underground. Watch yourself.

passages.title: Antifungal Firestarter
passages.text: Excellent work my friend. Dat will keep these beasts in check.

passages.title: Removing the Cap
passages.text:
Aemara's mention of a large fungarian planting fungal pods worries me. Gotta be someting down in dat cave.

We can't just be waitin' for the fungarians to attack with a nest of mind-controlled beasts. We gotta prune dat plan before it has a chance to bloom.

Get to Pillar-nest Vosh and kill that fungarian leader!

passages.title: Removing the Cap
passages.text: That fungarian leader's plans are over, and the camp is safe again. Thank you, friend.

passages.title: A Nebb in Need
passages.text:
You! You no spider. Please, must help before spiders come again. 

Nebb know Chittering Den. Never seen spiders here before. Eat grubs, eat kobolds. But spiders dark things from dark places. Hate light.

Can't leave post. You take candles, yes? Light up barricade. Keep spiders away.

passages.title: A Nebb in Need
passages.text: Keep away dark. Keep away spiders.

passages.title: A Nebb in Need
passages.text: Good. We safe for now.

passages.title: Hair of the Spider
passages.text:
Light good, but more to do. 

Spiders came from everywhere. Nebb quick, Nebb heard them. But friend Snubjaw... he bit. Sick now.

Nebb might know a way, yes, turn venom into cure. Use bite to cure bite.

Bring venom. Hurry now!

passages.title: Hair of the Spider
passages.text: You have venom?

passages.title: Hair of the Spider
passages.text: Yes, nasty venom make perfect cure.

passages.title: A Poultice for Poison
passages.text:
Little venom, little wax...

<Nebb reaches into his pouch and gives you a handful of thick, pungent wax.>

Yes, yes, should work. Finest poultice, family recipe. Hurry now, give to Snubjaw. He feel right better.

passages.title: A Poultice for Poison
passages.text: Poultice fix him right up.

passages.title: A Poultice for Poison
passages.text: No work, he worse! But why?

passages.title: A Royal Cure
passages.text:
Poultice no work! Wax right, venom wrong?

Yes... yes! Strongest cure need strongest venom. Nebb saw crawler. She queen in red and black, too big to bother with kobolds. Queen smelled juicy grubs and skittered for cave.

Now you must follow. Collect royal venom. Please, Snubjaw have little time.

passages.title: A Royal Cure
passages.text: Queen venom must work.

passages.title: A Royal Cure
passages.text: It work! He no green now. Thank you, thank you for saving friend Snubjaw.

passages.title: A Clutch of Hope
passages.text:
<The broodmother lies dead, coiled around a single egg. She gave her life to keep it from the spiders.

You should take it to Nebb. He and the other Grubtenders would know what to do with it.>

passages.title: A Clutch of Hope
passages.text: What this, another egg?

passages.title: A Clutch of Hope
passages.text:
This not just any egg. Mother egg.

<Nebb takes the egg from you. He holds it with reverence.>

With this, grubs not just survive. They thrive. Thank you. We protect.

passages.title: Charging Up That Hill
passages.text:
Before we use the conduit to summon the stormrooks, we need to recharge it. There are other, gentler ways to do this but... we have to work with what's on hand. 

The way to the peak is overrun with hostile elementals cast off from the storm. If we send them back to their plane, we can capture their residual energy and re-energize the conduit.

While you work on recharging the conduit, we will go ahead and prepare for the ritual at the peak.

passages.title: Charging Up That Hill
passages.text: Have you finished charging the conduit?

passages.title: Charging Up That Hill
passages.text:
The conduit! Do you feel that? It's humming--no, it's practically singing with power. 

I've heard this song before, late at night in the Stormperch's rookery. When the storms would come and lightning flashed across the bay, the rooks would answer just like this. 

You can't hear it?

passages.title: Heeding the Call
passages.text:
Earthen from across the island have been drawn to this place. Kind of a strange coincidence you'd show up now too.

Maybe it's because Baelgrim's gone or... a new Stormward's coming. Or it could just be barometric pressure...

Bah! There's time enough to spin wild theories later. Right now, we need to assist the pilgrims that have foolishly attempted the summit unprepared. We can't be worrying about them while we try to summon the stormrooks.

passages.title: Heeding the Call
passages.text: These earthen pilgrims seem intent on reaching the peak. I hope we can keep them safe.

passages.title: Heeding the Call
passages.text:
If the storm summoned these earthen here, does that mean they have a role to play in what comes next? 

We've directed them to hole up in the cave near the peak for now. I'm not sure what's next for them--or any of us.

passages.title: Strays
passages.text:
Kurdran Wildhammer has come to train the new Stormriders in aerial maneuvers. Thrall says his clan rides gryphons--much like the Stormriders ride stormrooks--so he should be of great help to us.

Unfortunately, a few of our new recruits seem to have, uh, wandered off with their stormrooks. I wanted them to have a chance to bond, but it's time to come home.

Would you mind rounding them up? Thrall and I are putting together something special for these "rookies" lessons.

passages.title: Strays
passages.text: You found those stray rookies yet?

passages.title: Strays
passages.text:
Right then! Good on ye for roundin' everyone up. We're lookin' tae start formal flight trainin' and we wouldn't want any stragglers, now would we? 

I'm eager to see what these stormrooks--and the earthen--can do.

passages.title: Paying Respects
passages.text:
Please excuse my absence. It was never my intention to turn my back on the Stormriders, then or now. But I needed to come here and pay my respects to Baelgrim.

Unfortunately, these blasted nerubians are still lingering. I think they're searching for something, but I don't know what. Whatever their reasons, I cannot abide them lurking where Baelgrim fell.

passages.title: Paying Respects
passages.text: I don't know who or what these nerubians are searching for, but they defile this place with their presence. Clear them out.

passages.title: Paying Respects
passages.text: This is a gift. Baelgrim may be gone, but his stormrook seems ready to carry on his fight. It's been a long time since I've felt such a connection. Such purpose. I don't intend to turn my back a second time.

passages.title: Tending to the Terrified
passages.text:
All happen so fast. One moment, we gathering eggs and grubs. Next, spiders swarming.

Nebb drag me here, many others trapped. Caught in webs, soon to be feasts. Must save the Grubtenders. 

We tenders, not fighters. Do not let friends become meals.

passages.title: Tending to the Terrified
passages.text: Aha, Grubtenders free! They survive to harvest again.

passages.title: Report to the Councilward
passages.text:
Those receipts you found... Steelvein is a known smuggler that we've been chasing for a long time. The Councilward will be pleased to finally have solid evidence on his activities, and maybe even on his whereabouts.

Bring these receipts to Merrix immediately. He will want to study them in detail. He said he was heading back to his office, so you should be able to find him at the Councilward's Rise.

I'll package up the rest of the evidence to be brought to him later. Good work today.

passages.title: Report to the Councilward
passages.text: <Seems like there is nothing else to do but leave the receipts on Merrix's desk.>

passages.title: Sedition
passages.text:
<The poster reads:>

MERRIX is CORRUPT! STEELVEIN is WEAK!

They cannot protect the earthen! They do not care about them! They spit upon the Edicts!

MERRIX was BRIBED to reopen Steelvein's smuggling operation! Steelvein HIDES behind MERRIX's authority!

They are taking from YOUR pockets to line THEIRS!

DO NOT TRUST THEIR LIES!

passages.title: Sedition
passages.text:
Yes, I am quite aware of the situation.

It has rather disrupted my morning.

passages.title: Forcing My Hand
passages.text:
I do not know if Ardgrin merely intended to sabotage me or if he wanted to force a confrontation. Either way, a confrontation he will have.

I believe this situation can be rectified peacefully, but I cannot do it as the Councilward. Steelvein has never appeared in the stone, but he must now. I will parlay with Ardgrin in the Deeps and this situation will be concluded.

I would have you accompany me, but there are some things I want you to know before that. Help me prepare and I will speak with you.

passages.title: Forcing My Hand
passages.text:
I will have this solved peacefully.

Though if Ardgrin asks for violence, we will answer.

passages.title: Bad Business
passages.text:
I have not been to the Deeps since their machines shut down. Obstorn will have to guide us to Ardgrin's depot.

Once there, I will attempt a conversation. If Ardgrin is not amenable, which I suspect will be the case, we will respond with equal force. Our goal is to bring him back into the fold, not to beat him into submission. Ruling by fear only breeds resentment.

We will meet you in the Deeps. Come swiftly--and, of course, speak of this to no one.

passages.title: Bad Business
passages.text:
Now that Ardgrin is willing to talk, we will talk. And all of this will be settled.

You have my gratitude, <name>.

passages.title: Smelly Shrubberies
passages.text:
Jenni here says she's got some creepers attackin' the goblins. I haven't seen any myself, but I do smell opportunity!

We've got our own anti-creeper perfume. It's the same recipe we use for the incense around town. Rub it on, and everything stays away! I'm sure we can sell some to the goblins.

But I'm out of materials--smellsage branches, specifically. If you gather some for me, I'll cut you in on the profits!

passages.title: Smelly Shrubberies
passages.text: If you smell feet, you're in the right spot.

passages.title: Smelly Shrubberies
passages.text: I could smell 'em the moment you came in! Those will work.

passages.title: Electrifying!
passages.text:
You wanna help the Venture Company? And you don't mind being disposable?

Okay, listen up. When we moved in here, there were no monsters in town. But now we're finding dead workers, chewed up. It's bad for business.

Fortunately, I've got a way to make money off this: an electrocution helmet. I call it my Debugger Hat.

Take the latest model for a test run outside town. Kill the bugs. The niffen will see you, see that Debugger Hat at work, and know it's got good reviews.

passages.title: Electrifying!
passages.text: It oughta just kill 'em, but who knows? You might see other results, too.

passages.title: Electrifying!
passages.text:
So it had some extra effects? Great! The hype is real! What exposure! The orders will be pouring in!

You ever consider becoming a walking advertisement? Could have a bright future in making cash for me. For now, here's your wages.

passages.title: The Party's Over
passages.text:
Nope, nope, nope!

Look, I'm used to dealing with the additives in our swimming hole and keeping things at "marginally safe" levels, but spiders emerging to chew us to death? That's a hard pass from me. 

This is OUR place, why are they buggin' us?

passages.title: The Party's Over
passages.text: We put an incense beacon in there to keep bugs out. If the goblins changed it...

passages.title: Burn It With Fire
passages.text:
So the goblins removed the incense the niffen used to keep those creepy pests out... because it smelled bad?

Honestly, I'm not surprised. Maybe we can show them that they need to work together. Leading by example! Here, I'll lend you a flamethrower. I know mine works, without weird... chicken-like effects.

Head in, clear out the nests, and put the right incense back in there!

passages.title: Burn It With Fire
passages.text: The cave is just up ahead.

passages.title: Burn It With Fire
passages.text: Okay, that flamethrower. I need it. I guess I'll talk to Gazlowe... but don't tell anyone that I did.

passages.title: Dornogal's Benefactor
passages.text:
You are in a unique position, <name>. A position to learn.

You met those who would bring this "Bender of Edicts" to justice, but what of the people of Dornogal? What do the earthen think of this Steelvein fellow? 

Humor me. Take the smuggled goods you intercepted and bring them to their intended recipients. Tell them the items are a gift from a "mutual friend."

You might be surprised to learn who benefits from these... illicit deeds.

passages.title: Dornogal's Benefactor
passages.text:
Harthan mentioned Ardgrin, you say?

He is a trade overseer from the Ringing Deeps. If he quarreled with Steelvein, that certainly concerns me.

passages.title: Holy Hydrocarbons
passages.text: These devotional candles might be of interest to Janky the kobold candlesmith in Gundargaz.

passages.title: Holy Hydrocarbons
passages.text: What smell like new candle?

passages.title: Holy Hydrocarbons
passages.text:
<Janky nibbles on one of the candles.>

Mhmm...mmm...fish oil...and touch of...sun blossom?

Interesting technique, yes!

passages.title: Deep Wax Galactic
passages.text:
While sourcing it may not be pleasant, this waxy substance seems like it might make a fine candle.

Janky the candlesmith in Gundargaz might be interested in this.

passages.title: Deep Wax Galactic
passages.text: What bring Janky?

passages.title: Deep Wax Galactic
passages.text:
Good bug wax, <name>! Make fancy bug candle out of this.

Scented, too!

passages.title: The Second Front
passages.text:
Our reinforcements are already inbound. 

These spiders just decided where our next wall will go. Clear a landing zone for General Steelstrike.

passages.title: The Second Front
passages.text: I will NOT risk the nerubians flanking us again. Their ambush is now our staging ground!

passages.title: Offensive Counter
passages.text:
I will not yield this ground. 

Get out there and kill anything with more than two legs!

passages.title: Offensive Counter
passages.text: Well done.

passages.title: Wipe Away Their Smiles
passages.text:
The kobyss grow bold if they feel they can defile our Veneration Grounds. I think we should collect their teeth to wipe the smiles off their faces.

Come! My brother and I will cleanse our lands from this filth. Try to keep up!

passages.title: Wipe Away Their Smiles
passages.text: Let's see them smile now!

passages.title: Wipe Away Their Smiles
passages.text:
A job well done, I think.

And you managed to keep up!

passages.title: Stave Them Off
passages.text:
Without their magical weapons, the kobyss casters won't be able to use their foul necromancy.

Steal their staves so we might toss them into the Sacred Flame and be done with them.

passages.title: Stave Them Off
passages.text: Did you find any Darkwater Staves?

passages.title: Stave Them Off
passages.text: Good job!

passages.title: Dreaded Dreadfang
passages.text:
My brother and I have dealt heavy blows to the kobyss, <name>, but you could have done more. 

The most foul kobyss of them all has yet to taste my blade. If we take out their leader, the rest will flee back into the waters from which they came.

Let's take the head of Dreadfang!

passages.title: Dreaded Dreadfang
passages.text: Ready to kill some kobyss?

passages.title: Dreaded Dreadfang
passages.text: No, please! Get up! ... Theleon...

passages.title: Go to the Priory
passages.text:
I... I do not have the words. Theleon...

I will take h-his body. They will know what to do at the priory.

Oh, brother... It was not supposed to end like this...

passages.title: Go to the Priory
passages.text: So young to have been taken from us. So brave and bold. Perhaps too bold.

passages.title: Memorial Wine
passages.text:
Oh, Theleon. He always did follow his big brother into anything. 

While we prepare Theleon for his final rest, would you please help Brother Abealard with a batch of Memorial Wine for the service?

passages.title: Memorial Wine
passages.text: Did you help Brother Abealard?

passages.title: Memorial Wine
passages.text: Such a shame we need to make so much of this wine.

passages.title: Priory of the Sacred Flame: A Brother's Grief
passages.text:
I fear that the Prioress may be behind our missing dead-- and our missing baron. Sybaestan has disappeared as well and I don't believe in coincidences. 

She and Sybaestan have taken our recent losses hard. I fear what their overwhelming grief might be doing to their souls. We must confront them and bring them back to sanity... If we can.

Tell General Steelstrike what you have learned. We might need her backup. I'll be waiting for you here.

passages.title: Priory of the Sacred Flame: A Brother's Grief
passages.text: We must confront the prioress.

passages.title: Priory of the Sacred Flame: A Brother's Grief
passages.text: I wish it could have happened some other way... but at last they are all at peace.

passages.title: Trade Partners
passages.text:
Have you visited Mmarl? It's a trade town to the southeast of here. 

Try some of Corby's barbeque while you're over there!

passages.title: Trade Partners
passages.text: Hey there <name>! Thanks for catchin' up with me.

passages.title: Muddled Mind in the Mine
passages.text:
The workers said they saw Munderut near the back of the mining area. Please find him and tell him that I said he needs to report back in. 

He might not remember me, or that I am his fused. Tell him to look down at his chest, at the medallion he wears. His memory of our time together fades in and out these days, but the medallion tells of our story and bond forever.

passages.title: Muddled Mind in the Mine
passages.text:
Who are you? What are you doing here? 

Actually, what was I doing here? Gathering spines, I suppose. I got distracted by all the elementals. They have made this area quite dangerous. I'm more of an artist than a fighter.

passages.title: Monsters in the Dark
passages.text:
The local quarry was an active source of clay and ore for us until the fungarians took over some time ago.

We were worried about the fungarians encroaching upon the village, but there's something more.

Multiple sightings of a creature much larger than our native wildlife have been reported at night.

Combined with villager Modhina's disappearance, I fear this is no coincidence. She visited the quarry recently and hasn't returned.

We would be in your debt if you searched the tunnels.

passages.title: Monsters in the Dark
passages.text: You do us a great service by making our lands safe.

passages.title: Monsters in the Dark
passages.text:
A stonestalker, here? Their habitat resides far beneath the isle's surface. All the recent change must be disturbing them.

Regardless, thank you for slaying it. They are highly territorial and kill for sport.

As for the tunnels, the area sounds beyond recovery. We'll have to let nature reclaim it.

passages.title: Buried, Not Forgotten
passages.text:
Several suns ago, my friend Modhina ventured into the quarry cave. She wanted to find rare ore for Hreka, to help her craftsmanship. Modhina was excited, I remember. A rare feeling for earthen.

She hasn't returned. The fungarians prevent us from searching the area.

It would mean a great deal to us if you could look for her. I didn't know it was possible to spend so much of the day thinking about what if's.

passages.title: Buried, Not Forgotten
passages.text: Be careful. I fear more sinister things lurk in these tunnels.

passages.title: Buried, Not Forgotten
passages.text: You've returned! Did you find Modhina...? What is all that you are carrying?

passages.title: A Titanic Expedition!
passages.text:
Our merchant friend told us about some small islands off the northeast coast called "The Three Shields."

Apparently, there was a lot of titan activity there long ago. To me, the "activity" sounded like titan research and development. Exciting stuff!

Tuberros and I are going there to check it out. Tharessa, my new Algari Expedition trainee, is coming along to see true professionals at work.

Care to join us?

passages.title: A Titanic Expedition!
passages.text:
All right, I'm fine. It's just a scratch. 

But it took the three of us to bring down one little gorloc, so it's good you decided to join us.

passages.title: Not a Heating Pack
passages.text:
Tharessa has done some reconnaissance for us and found the gorlocs are digging up artifacts and... cuddling with them. 

I think it means that the artifacts emit heat? Maybe that means some artifacts are still functioning?

Imagine--the titans created technology to shape worlds, and now a fish uses it to warm their fins. Hah!

The gorlocs won't give them up, and I don't want to be a Rannan-kabob either. I hate to ask because they just want to be warm, but could you do something about them?

passages.title: Not a Heating Pack
passages.text: Did you get them? I thought I saw one sneak by a moment ago...

passages.title: Not a Heating Pack
passages.text: Wonderful! Now we can focus our attention on what really matters--the artifacts. I wonder what we will discover?

passages.title: "Cataloguing"
passages.text:
As ya know, we are here to collect some titan shinies, artifacts, whatever!

And Rannan thinks the more shinies--er, you know what I mean--the better chance we have figurin' out something about the titans.

That'll make Rannan happy, but it'll also ensure I have some extras to take to my store back home.

My wife, Perisimona, is waiting for 'em back in Loamm. I can't go back empty handed!

passages.title: "Cataloguing"
passages.text: You get some good shinies yet?

passages.title: "Cataloguing"
passages.text:
<Tuberros looks at the titan artifacts.>

This one smells very acidic--and it's broken. I can take it to the store... Rannan would like to see that one... Oh yeah, these are great. Thank you for bringing them to me.

passages.title: Because It's Shiny
passages.text:
While these two were ordering you around, I thought I would do something useful and make sure the gorlocs were not going to surprise us here on the beach.

None of them seemed interested in us, but then I saw one huge gorloc.

It killed off some smaller gorlocs then took off. It had something glowing in its claw though!

It had to be an artifact. And it looked like it was working! We've got to get it back.

By "we" I mean "you." Larger-than-average gorlocs are above my Dragonscale pay grade.

passages.title: Because It's Shiny
passages.text: Were you able to get the artifact?

passages.title: Because It's Shiny
passages.text:
I can hear it humming from here. Ow. It irritates my ears.

Let's see if our two "professionals," Rannan and Tuberros, know what this artifact is.

passages.title: It's Probably Nothing
passages.text:
You found a buzz orb! 

...Er, that's what the niffen call it. I just kind of went with it. 

It's still in a good condition. Still buzzing, humming, and warm to the touch! I haven't seen one since we were in Zaralek Cavern!

<name>, you should see if we can get it to work. I will stand back here, just in case it is, um, not friendly. 

Nothing to worry about, I'm sure.

passages.title: It's Probably Nothing
passages.text: Yes, yes! It will be very exciting to hear what you have discovered.

passages.title: It's Probably Nothing
passages.text:
Alpha site? Defense grid?

I don't like the sound of that.

We should get going. I don't want to be here if its friends come back with it.

That's not a reunion party I want to be a part of.

Hopefully it won't hone in on Tharessa... Nah, probably not. Anyway, we should get going. Like now.

Catch you later, <name>. Thanks for your... um, help? I guess?

passages.title: Raging Rifts
passages.text:
The elementals are coming from inside that cave. We only made it part of the way in before needing to retreat. 

I could see some flickering within, some strange glowing thing that looked almost like a tear in space from which the elementals poured forth! We managed to close one of these portals, but there are more.

I need to stay with Nanthaz. It is up to you now, if you can manage. Destroy the rifts and find their source. I suspect it lies deeper within the cave.

passages.title: Raging Rifts
passages.text:
Destroy what rifts you come across, but above all, find their source! I suspect you will find it deep inside the nearby cave.

The miners you rescued spoke of breaking through to a crystal-filled room, and of the elementals pouring forth from within.

passages.title: Raging Rifts
passages.text:
You return with good news, I hope? 

<You tell her about Urthgrafr Riftcaller.>

With Urthgrafr's defeat, we should have no problem cleaning up the rest of the elementals and rifts ourselves. We are lucky that you came along when you did.

Thank you for your help, friend. Do not worry about me or Nanthaz. We will make our way back to the refinery once he has caught his breath. Gratitude, outlander. And may all earthen Awaken one day.

passages.title: ...And Now I'm Arachnophobic
passages.text:
Who is there? Someone? Did I imagine you?

I am Albert. I was a Pathfinder once. Now that I'm blind, I see no path. It seems wrong to call myself Pathfinder Henson. I can hear, though. I can hear them eating. They eat the fresh parts.

My eyes. My insides.

It hurts all the time. They do not want my rotten pieces. The decayed parts are all I have left. The worst of me. 

I wasn't alone here, I had fellow Pathfinders. I keep hearing sobbing from the walls. Do you hear them too?

passages.title: ...And Now I'm Arachnophobic
passages.text: They are dead, then...

passages.title: Legs in the Ceiling
passages.text:
I don't require vengeance on my behalf, but I would like vengeance for all of my friends that were eaten. I didn't think the Horror of Xesh was real, but she is. Xishirra. A shadow of a nightmare, making a brood of monsters while she stays out of reach.

The horror is ancient, and beyond us, but we can still make her pay! Pull hard on a web strand if you need to, and deal with whatever comes. We'll escape after some justice is had!

passages.title: Legs in the Ceiling
passages.text: <Albert's eyes were already dark, but any spark of life has faded from the rest of him, as well.>

passages.title: Maggots in your Eyes
passages.text:
<Albert is no longer alive. All that remains is his head, still full of maggots.

Taking him back to the Pathfinders seems like the right thing to do.>

passages.title: Maggots in your Eyes
passages.text: Whose head is that?

passages.title: Maggots in your Eyes
passages.text:
This eyeless, mostly eaten, maggot-infested head is...

Albert! Oh no, what happened?!

We didn't know where his team had gone, just that they'd taken a mission near the city.  I can't imagine the trauma he endured, or what you had to do to bring his remains to us. We'll take it from here. Thank you for bringing him back.

And I hope the nightmares that could come from this don't linger for you, friend.

passages.title: A Wrench in the Works
passages.text:
Looks like the High Speaker is addressing his workers. It seems something has finally shaken them from their complacency, and their time away from the Awakening Machine is affecting them.

<Moira pauses to brush a bit of dust off her robe.>

Perhaps this would be a good opportunity for everyone to hear what they have to say?

We should convince a few of these Machine Speakers to speak up.

passages.title: A Wrench in the Works
passages.text: Recalcitrant lot, aren't they?

passages.title: A Wrench in the Works
passages.text: Excellent, now we're starting to make some progress.

passages.title: The Last Mage
passages.text:
I want you to check in on someone. He's a mage... the only one of us who is. All the others died in the crash.

He's trying to make a portal to the Empire, so we can get reinforcements and have a way to and from home. 

We all know it's a lost cause, but he still hasn't given up. 

Maybe meeting a seasoned traveler like you will give him the reality check he needs. Check on him, will you?

passages.title: The Last Mage
passages.text:
What? Who sent you? 

It doesn't matter, listen! I'm so close to a breakthrough I can taste it!

passages.title: Arcane Trickles
passages.text:
I've almost got it!

I'm making a new kind of teleportation spell to get us back home to the Empire.

These crabs might just be the key. They're practically radiating arcane teleportation magic!

I need more samples to study. 

Take this focus, it will let you see traces of the arcane. There aren't many other arcane sources around here, so any you see should lead you straight to the affected crabs!

passages.title: Arcane Trickles
passages.text: Have you found the crabs? They'll be near water. That focus should let you see the trails of arcane dust they leave behind.

passages.title: Arcane Trickles
passages.text: Yes, these are perfect!

passages.title: Arcane Experiments
passages.text:
This is it! The energy crackling from these crabs is charged with teleportation magic! I just need to extract it and adjust the formula--

I can do this, my new friend! I just need another hand. Help me test this?

passages.title: Arcane Experiments
passages.text: <Wenren's lifeless eyes stare up at you.>

passages.title: A Murder Most Foul
passages.text:
<Somebody didn't want Wenren to finish his spell.

Find out who.>

passages.title: A Murder Most Foul
passages.text: <The body is still warm.>

passages.title: A Murder Most Foul
passages.text: <You carefully consider the clues you have gathered.>

passages.title: Finding Justice
passages.text:
<The pieces fit together to form a simple, but dark picture.

The Order of Night did not want Wenren to create a portal back to the Empire. No doubt reinforcements and supplies would hinder their mission. 

So, someone stabbed him, burned his research, and smashed his tools. 

But with this arcane focus in hand, you can see a faint trail of arcane residue. Did some arcane dust get on the perpetrator? 

Follow the trail and find out.>

passages.title: Finding Justice
passages.text:
<Steelstrike listens to your story with growing concern.>

No! Dead?!

passages.title: Social Clues
passages.text:
<The nerubian keeps her voice low, a careful eye on the guards behind you.>

The Weaver sent you, yes? I arrived to petition the Magistrate's approval for Ascension--to infiltrate high society, of course.

But he's missing. A rather large inconvenience.

I need to ask around. You're just what I've been waiting for! You may pretend to be my... servant. Pet? Whatever makes it more palatable to you.

I so rarely get to work alongside a friend. We will have fun together, fellow spy.

passages.title: Social Clues
passages.text:
I have a few old friends who recently Ascended. Surely, one of them has heard something they would be willing to share. For old time's sake.

And if not, maybe jealousy in seeing my fashionable new pet will inspire them to offer up what they know.

passages.title: Social Clues
passages.text:
I knew Ascension changed people, but... They were my friends. And now, they don't even want to be seen with me.

It makes me wonder... if I succeed in all this, will I even still be myself?

<Tx'itk shakes her head.>

It doesn't matter. I'll do what needs to be done.

passages.title: Pulling Strings
passages.text:
Just think of it! Overcrawlers, war prisoners, civilians, fellow nerubians, important nobility being kidnapped and turned into puppets right under the Magistrate's nose.

It's horrific--and exactly what I needed! If we save the Magistrate from this fate, he'll owe me. Not just for saving his life, but to keep quiet about all this.

We're off to the theater, then. If you can keep the Puppetmaster occupied, I'll free High Elevator Etak'kaht from his grasp.

Hopefully he's not part of the show yet.

passages.title: Pulling Strings
passages.text:
I'm thrilled. There couldn't have been a more perfect opportunity to get the Magistrate's attention. And the Weaver will be pleased to hear we have him in our pocket indefinitely, with this blackmail situation.

Now, I suppose I'm off to the Transformatory.

<Tx'itk shudders subtly.>

I... I must not let my resolve falter now. The Weaver has asked this of me. I will be her eyes.

passages.title: How Scandalous!
passages.text:
Did you see anything?

I was just at the Forgegrounds picking up a jewelry commission and all of a sudden everyone was shouting like the Coreway was under attack--again.

But it was not that...

Some peacekeepers were heading towards the depot--where crafting shipments are sent up from the Deeps. I bet it's something to do with the machine speakers!

The peacekeepers ushered everyone away before I could see what had happened. But maybe you can sneak a glimpse?

passages.title: How Scandalous!
passages.text:
Move along. This is an ongoing--Oh, <name>, my apologies.

We may actually need your assistance.

passages.title: An Oddball in Dornogal
passages.text:
We have received reports that an eccentric Arathi is accosting our citizens. We have little experience with outsiders and my superiors are wary of a diplomatic incident.

I have been tasked with finding this "Lamplighter" and resolving his concerns. You have worked with the Arathi before - can you assist me?

I have a list of earthen who have reported the Lamplighter. You can interview half the list. Between us, we can hopefully locate the Arathi before he troubles more citizens.

passages.title: An Oddball in Dornogal
passages.text:
This is not quite what I was expecting.

He is certainly odd but a troublemaker? I think not.

passages.title: Found Around the Unbound
passages.text:
This Lamplighter is looking for his fellow Arathi. The foreman says he directed an Arathi shipwright to Freywold Village.

My superiors insist that Peacekeepers do not leave Dornogal... but per their orders, I must assist Kaerter. And to do that, I have no choice but to leave the city.

<Leif quickly hides a smile.>

It is decided then. If you are willing, please meet us at Freywold Village. Your continued aid would be appreciated.

passages.title: Found Around the Unbound
passages.text:
It seems the locals have taken issue with our foreign companion. I am attempting to defuse the situation as best I can.

But we have more pressing problems.

passages.title: The Abductors' Obstructors
passages.text:
The Order of Night is clearly interested in our resources. They have abducted earthen to harvest for them and may continue taking others. We must stop them.

The next largest earthen settlement is Rambleshire. If the Order needs more workers, they might have gone there to get them.

Go on ahead <name>. I must first speak with Kaerter about why the Arathi are doing this.

passages.title: The Abductors' Obstructors
passages.text:
While we have not yet seen any Arathi, there is an uneasiness about the town.

Kaerter believes the Order is here. He says they are simply waiting for a moment to strike.

passages.title: Holy Fire in Rambleshire
passages.text:
I'm certain there are still Order folks sneaking around here. Now they might be carrying messages on them, just like the clues you found in Freywold. 

You and I are gonna find out.

Here, take these thuribles. They might look like tiny incense burners, but I've enchanted them with Sacred Flame. 

Just throw one down and you'll get a big bang with a bright flash! Should be enough to stun anyone sneaking around. 

Just don't throw one at me! Got it?

passages.title: Holy Fire in Rambleshire
passages.text:
Alright, I'll admit it, the little Pebble is pretty useful. He knows more about the earthen and the surface than I ever will. 

Anyway, did you find anything?

passages.title: Holy Fire in Rambleshire
passages.text:
"New friends" huh?

Guess I'm not the only one...

<Kaerter freezes when he realizes what he's just said and suddenly points a finger at you.>

You didn't hear me say nothing, got it?

passages.title: A Time to Kill at the Lumber Mill
passages.text:
Alright, let me see if I get all of this. The shipwright brings an entourage up here to get lumber for airships. 

But the shipwright is actually Order of Night, along with most of her group. So they murder the loyal Arathi, kidnap earthen, and force them to run the lumber mill up here.

And now we gotta deal with the Order AND whoever their new friends are.

<Kaerter swears and shakes his head.>

C'mon, let's head to the mill. We got a lot of bad guys to kill and time's wastin'.

passages.title: A Time to Kill at the Lumber Mill
passages.text:
Nerubians. Lots and lots of nerubians.

By Beledar's Light do I hate nerubians.

passages.title: Ungirthin' the Earthen
passages.text:
While I do enjoy beating the black blood out of nerubians, we must save the earthen prisoners first.

I saw they're being held by Arathi ball and chain. Someone like you should be able to shatter them pretty quick. Just... do that thing you do!

Oh, and we should split up to cover more ground. Yeah Leif's gonna complain, but he's always complaining anyway.

passages.title: Ungirthin' the Earthen
passages.text: Well done. I will lead the few I was able to rescue to safety.

passages.title: Concealed in the Weald
passages.text:
The nerubians seem to be in league with the Arathi. Many of them are guarding the mill, but I am sure there are more than we can see.

We cannot allow such a large enemy force to operate unimpeded this close to Rambleshire.

The nerubians attacked and destroyed large sections of Dornogal not too long ago. The Order of Night Arathi are abducting and enslaving our people.

We must eliminate as many of them as we can. Preferably all of them.

passages.title: Concealed in the Weald
passages.text: The more enemies we eliminate, the safer we will all be.

passages.title: Concealed in the Weald
passages.text: That should disrupt their operation. Let us hope it is enough for now.

passages.title: A Lamplight for the Shipwright
passages.text:
Where is Kaerter now? Did he go off on his own again?

<Leif sighs.>

We've rescued the earthen and eliminated many hostile forces, but our task is not yet complete.

Shortly before you arrived, we spotted a group of Arathi traveling up this hill. One of them was identified as the Arathi shipwright.

The shipwright is the leader here. Losing her will cripple their efforts to utilize the mill.

Head up the hill and find her before she can escape.

passages.title: A Lamplight for the Shipwright
passages.text: Kaerter is injured. He will not be an effective fighter until he heals.

passages.title: Up to No Good Down in Silkwood
passages.text:
The Order is moving the wood through the nerubians. Leif said he saw the shipwright leave the cave and head down to the beach. 

The nerubian tunnel must be down there. You're going to have to seal that Flameforsaken passage.

While slinking around, I noticed the Order brought explosive barrels with them. Find a few and use them to blow the tunnel.

Get going <name>. I'll be right behind you.

passages.title: Up to No Good Down in Silkwood
passages.text: Did you take out the tunnel?

passages.title: Up to No Good Down in Silkwood
passages.text:
Good stuff <name>. That should put a dent in their plans!

With that tunnel gone, ain't no way for them to send that wood to Hallowfall now. That makes the mill all but worthless.

Phew! Order stopped, earthen saved, nerubians killed. Job well done if you ask me!

I don't know 'bout you, but I could use a vacation.

passages.title: Gasping Plea
passages.text:
<A gasping, pathetic-looking fish taken from the corpse of a kobyss flops weakly in your hand. Its beady eye twitches, and you suddenly hear a breathless voice in the recesses of your mind.>

The water. Take me to the water. Away from these kobyss wretches. Away from the sky.

passages.title: Gasping Plea
passages.text:
<The fish gulps down saltwater to regain its breath and then turns to look at you with intelligent eyes.>

I live, thanks to you. The shade of these rocks suits me nicely for the work to be done. 

Allow me to repay your selfless gesture.

passages.title: Tidal Charms
passages.text:
<When the fish speaks, its lips do not move. You hear its voice in your head.>

No doubt you have found that your senses cannot be trusted when dealing with the kobyss. A tremendous power, is it not? It is only fair that you show them the power they wield is not theirs alone.

I will show you how to craft a tool to lure and destroy them. You will find their kind carry shards taken from the deep. Bring them to me.

passages.title: Tidal Charms
passages.text: Bring the materials. Only then can we continue.

passages.title: Tidal Charms
passages.text: Glinting abyssal shards and strands of coral. Bound with words of power and worn around the neck, I will show you how to trick the senses of your enemies.

passages.title: Voices from the Deep
passages.text:
To deceive the senses of these kobyss is one matter. To know what will captivate them is another. They champ and drool at the thought of devouring your kind. But it is the voices of the deep that transfix them and lower their guard. It's then that you will strike.

Search their shrines to gain an insight for what these wretches hold sacred. See how they have twisted the bellowing truths that lie below.

passages.title: Voices from the Deep
passages.text: What have you learned?

passages.title: Voices from the Deep
passages.text: You see now what the kobyss revere. It is time to put that dark knowledge to use.

passages.title: Alluring Offer
passages.text:
It is done. Take this tidal charm, cloak your form in the darkness of the sea, and unmake the kobyss. Their strongest warriors gather and scheme against your kind upon that central island. With the lure, they will not see you for what you are. Use that advantage to become their end.

But understand, as the kobyss fail to, this is a power you borrow. It belongs to the sea.

passages.title: Alluring Offer
passages.text: Isolate them. Destroy them.

passages.title: Alluring Offer
passages.text:
With this, the lesson has been given. They will think twice before considering my kind as meat.

You kill well, land-walker. But the power of the deep must be returned. Our time together nears its end.

passages.title: Return to the Sea
passages.text: I remain weakened by my time so near the searing Light of the surface. I ask that you take me to deeper waters, away from these kobyss, where I can return to my kind.

passages.title: Return to the Sea
passages.text:
<A warbling cry emanates from the fish. It casts its song into the ocean depths.>

I expected an ignoble end at the hands of the kobyss for my folly. Never could I have believed a land-dweller would be my savior. I will remember you. Now, let the facade be at its end. My kind will be expecting me.

<The fish's form begins to shift and unwind. You realize its guise as a fish has been yet another illusion.>

passages.title: Departure
passages.text:
Best if we split up here. I'll guide everyone to safety and see about getting them evacuated.

In the meantime, you should search for Khadgar. I'm sure he could use your aid as well.

You'll find another exit further ahead that should lead back to the surface.

passages.title: Departure
passages.text: <The portal flickers and twists, making it impossible to see through to the other side.>

passages.title: Shattered Spires
passages.text:
With nothing to contain their arcane power, Dalaran's spires are crumbling.

If we let their energies continue to bleed out unchecked, that power could destabilize and destroy what is left of our forces.

Find Aethas! He will know what to do.

passages.title: Shattered Spires
passages.text:
Jaina yet lives?

Thank the Sunwell!

Though none of us will survive long if we do not contain the energies of the spires.

passages.title: A Light of the Dark
passages.text:
The image of a purple candle, burning with glorious power springs unbidden to your mind as you contemplate the decaying filth before you, followed by a faint whisper echoing through your mind: "One candle to rule them all, and in its brightness bind them."

Bring Janky the candlesmith in Gundargaz enough Coagulated Black Blood to forge a most unfortunate candle.

passages.title: A Light of the Dark
passages.text:
<Janky shivers as you approach.>

Ah!

passages.title: A Light of the Dark
passages.text: Oh...Janky not normally turn down new candle, but you sure?

passages.title: The Caretaker of Brunwin's Terrace
passages.text:
Greetings, outlander. You must be the problem solver I've heard about! I'm Caretaker Batzvara. I tend to earthen who have gone into stasis, like our friend here.

I often patrol Brunwin's Terrace to honor my fellow earthen with an offering of cinderbrew. Recently, however, I've drawn the attention of a local species of moles. They have a nose for sweets, and greedy claws for all else.

You look like you can defend yourself. Will you accompany me to pay respect to those who have gone into stasis?

passages.title: The Caretaker of Brunwin's Terrace
passages.text: Gratitude expressed. Your reputation as a stalwart ally is well-deserved.

passages.title: Shimmermist Falls
passages.text:
West of Gundargaz is another green space - a lovely area with waterfalls and more terraces. My schedule takes me in that direction next, and I would be very glad of your company to help deal with the wildlife there as well. 

If your other duties are not pressing, let us meet there.

passages.title: Shimmermist Falls
passages.text: You made it! Let us get to work.

passages.title: Into the Deeps
passages.text:
Onward and downward it is, then. We'd best follow after Speaker Brinthe and see what state the nerubians have left her home in.

Magni, Dagran, and I will accompany you down in due time. Would you mind roving ahead and making sure there's a warm welcome awaiting us?

passages.title: Into the Deeps
passages.text: By the Titans! It looks like the nerubians did a number on our station... but I see no spidery fiends here. Only struggling Machine Speakers...

passages.title: A Sassy Arathi
passages.text:
I had heard that an Arathi was making trouble in the city. It sounds like he is butting heads with the peacekeepers.

You've worked with the Arathi before, haven't you? Maybe you'd be able to smooth over any ruffled feathers.

passages.title: A Sassy Arathi
passages.text: Yes, how can I help you?

passages.title: The Bronzebeard Family
passages.text:
<Moira takes a deep, centering breath.>

We need to let Brann and my son Dagran know what happened. They're at Dalaran's visitor center.

Could ye go get them for me? Father needs his family right now.

passages.title: The Bronzebeard Family
passages.text:
My son always has been the scholarly sort. Takes after his father in that way...

We're all quite proud of him.

passages.title: The Bronzebeard Family
passages.text:
It's good for us to all be in one room together, even if the reason is so dire. My father hasn't really been a... part of Dagran's life. But I mean to change that, you have my word.

Thank ye, <name>.

passages.title: Don't Cry for Me, Azj-Kahet
passages.text:
<You find a crumpled page of journal paper wrapped around a small key.>

I always suspected Arax'ne was a traditionalist, but I didn't think she'd go this far. I don't know where I'm going, but I just have to get away from her.

To whoever finds this, it means the worst has come to pass. This key unlocks a chest that contains all my worldly possessions. They are yours.

All I ask is that you avenge me by slaying Arax'ne.

passages.title: Don't Cry for Me, Azj-Kahet
passages.text: The key glints silver in the light of Azj-Kahet.

passages.title: Don't Cry for Me, Azj-Kahet
passages.text:
The contents of this chest now belong to you.

--Klaskin

passages.title: Dread in the Den
passages.text:
You kobold friend, yes? Need help. Bad things happening in the Chittering Den. 

Glumtooth Gang setting up camp. Cronies of Candle King, want war with earthen.

Can't stop them alone. Meet me at camp.

passages.title: Dread in the Den
passages.text: You came. Good. Much to do. Much to protect.

passages.title: Healing the Headwaters
passages.text: Glumtooth Gang so wasteful! They leave much scrap in the water. Bad for water. Bad for scrap. Go clean it up.

passages.title: Healing the Headwaters
passages.text: Much better. Make no sense to let scrap rot in pool.

passages.title: Break out Berrund!
passages.text:
You work good. Now they let you into ring to "fight" earthen. You go to ring when ready. Cinder-flash candles could go off any moment.

I head back to camp. Wait for you and earthen there.

You good one. No get killed.

passages.title: Break out Berrund!
passages.text: Captured? No, I was just gathering information. And I've got bad news.

passages.title: Bump off the Boss
passages.text:
That kobold knows her stuff. Scrit says Boss Whiskerlash has his own cadre of spiders in a cave nearby. Don't worry, I'll lead the charge. 

Come on, we've got a boss to take down.

passages.title: Bump off the Boss
passages.text:
You back! Berrund came back alone. Scrit worried.

It done then? Good. Glumtooth Gang no last long without leader.

passages.title: Resounding Repercussions
passages.text:
I did not mean for...

<Orweyna's eyes narrow.>

Fetch him, <name>. You were exposed to the Black Blood, too. But Hannan took most of it.

He has entered the Unseeming, his mind shifted to a realm beyond our eyes through exposure to the Black Blood. You may need to join him, however far in he ventured, to retrieve him.

I will activate the nerubian cleansing instrument for when you return.

Do not lose yourself in that altered state.

passages.title: Resounding Repercussions
passages.text: Is this real? Am I imagining the monsters?

passages.title: Resounding Repercussions
passages.text: My head... It hurts. Everything feels so cloudy and... Help, please!

passages.title: Enemies Abound
passages.text:
<Hannan is barely responsive and less corporeal than he should be, lost deeper in the Unseeming than you.>

Some of the canisters exploded... Then the spiders appeared.

Kill the--kill the spiders!

passages.title: Enemies Abound
passages.text: Hmm. I have noticed you seem good at surviving challenging tasks. I will remember this about you.

passages.title: Song of Restoring
passages.text:
<Orweyna looks relieved at the sight of Hannan, but does not seem dissuaded from her task.>

I cannot say I am surprised at what you found in that cave. Nerubians stuck in the Unseeming, trapped in a realm of monsters and madness...

I would pity them, but they sought this out.

You, however, need to shift back before the influence of the Black Blood becomes too strong on your mind.

passages.title: Song of Restoring
passages.text:
It is a relief that the tuning crystal we found worked on this strange instrument. For once we should be grateful for the ingenuity of the nerubians.

If this device had not worked, we may have been stuck in the Unseeming forever. Like the nerubians in the cave.

passages.title: Song of Restoring
passages.text:
She can't keep running off like this! The rest of us followed her here--against our better judgement I might add--but we never agreed to...

<Hannan sighs.>

No, we knew exactly what we were getting into with her. And the... consequences.

passages.title: Staunch the Flow
passages.text:
Do they even understand what they are doing?

<Orweyna bares her teeth, practically growling.>

Destroy as many of those extractors as you can. Shatter the bulbs, snap the limbs, burn the wreckage.

We cannot stop them all, not today. But a bit of destruction may temper my rage.

passages.title: Staunch the Flow
passages.text:
They have already done so much damage. The creatures that once lived here, the earth that once thrived...

If we cannot stop them, we will take vengeance for that which they've destroyed beyond repair.

passages.title: Listener Lost
passages.text:
Blast it all! 

Brennok and I were on our way to Shadowvein Point to conduct a recitation ceremony. We were attacked by scorpids. Now the hauler has a scorpid stinger lodged in its gears, and Brennok wandered off.

He said he was going to stretch his legs while I fixed the hauler, but that was a while ago. I need to get the bot moving again, can you look for him?

passages.title: Listener Lost
passages.text: You don't understand, I was going to leave the Ringing Deeps. But I can't now, not without my book!

passages.title: The Common Costume
passages.text:
I'll slip away after the recitation. It's easy to vanish in a crowd of earthen enjoying a keg of cinderbrew.

However, I can't be recognized when I leave town. I don't want anyone to stop me. Or worse, to think I'm abandoning my oath. Better to just disappear.

If you find me a spare set of Miner's Clothes, I'll be able to get away without being noticed.

passages.title: The Common Costume
passages.text: Did you find them yet?

passages.title: The Common Costume
passages.text: Thank you. No one should recognize me in these.

passages.title: Eyes of the Weaver
passages.text:
The Weaver's many eyes lurk throughout the city, learning as much as they can about Ansurek's machinations.

Still, intelligence enough will not be sufficient to turn the tide against the Sureki forces. The Weaver requires someone willing to get their hands dirty.

Lucky you, I suppose.

passages.title: Eyes of the Weaver
passages.text: Chk-chaah! You return at least. What news of the city do you bring me, hrm?

passages.title: Eyes of the Weaver
passages.text:
You have big talent for causing good trouble! Good good!

Take these!

passages.title: Blade of the General
passages.text:
Even now, General Anub'azal's forces work tirelessly to ensure the security of Azj-Kahet.

Ansurek's reach extends to every corner of her domain. The General seeks to undermine her military authority. If we stretch her resources thin, then we may find new opportunities to strike.

passages.title: Blade of the General
passages.text: Hrmph. It is about time that you've returned. What news?

passages.title: Blade of the General
passages.text:
You have returned alive, and the enemies of Anub'azal have not. 

That is cause enough for recognition!

passages.title: Hand of the Vizier
passages.text:
The Vizier works even now to spread our conspiracy's influence amongst the well-to-do of Azj-Kahet's elite. Given his position, though, he can offer little in the way of direct support.

That is where you come in. Your growing reputation precedes you; you can move in ways that the Vizier cannot. Just take care not to get eaten, hrm?

passages.title: Hand of the Vizier
passages.text: I fear that our task grows more arduous with each passing day. I hope you are not wasting time.

passages.title: Hand of the Vizier
passages.text:
Thanks to your efforts, the Vizier is one step closer to parity with the enemy. 

For that, thanks are necessary.

passages.title: Defragmenting Memory
passages.text:
My oath is to be a compiler. I collect and tell the stories of our people.

<Brennok sighs.>

Is there wisdom in stories told by someone who never lived them? I've never had an adventure. I was afraid to overwrite the stories entrusted to me.

So I started transcribing them into a book I hid here. Each time we returned to Shadowvein Point, I added more.

I was going to leave and pass on the book, but scorpids ransacked it. Please, find the missing pages before they stuff them into their nests.

passages.title: Defragmenting Memory
passages.text: Thousands of stories, now they're probably lining some animal's den...

passages.title: Defragmenting Memory
passages.text:
By the Titans, thank you! I don't know what I would have done if I'd lost these. 

I can finally leave without failing my oath.

passages.title: Stuffed Lynx Toy
passages.text: Mr. Skinny! I thought you were lost forever!

passages.title: Broken Bracelet
passages.text:
That is... 

<Keyrra carefully places the bracelet in her palm.>

I can't believe it.

passages.title: One Last Story
passages.text:
Well, it's time. I'll be holding the recitation at the mine entrance. I'll see you there, though don't feel obligated to stay the whole time.

I'll leave my book for Haimaz to find. She'll take care of it.

After the ceremony, I would like to say goodbye properly. Meet me by the bridge outside of town. I'll head there after the recitation.

passages.title: One Last Story
passages.text:
I knew Brennok was acting odd. Then one of the miners mentioned you'd borrowed a spare set of clothes. That and his strange mood, well, it wasn't hard to guess that he planned to leave.

I expected him to come this way, though. Have you seen him?

passages.title: Tending to Ausgazur
passages.text:
Assigned tasks complete! I'll check back on these folks on my next scheduled patrol.

There is one more earthen I must tend to today. He was... he is very special to me.

You've been an especially considerate colleague, so I'd like for you to see him. Let us travel west a bit, closer to the falls.

passages.title: Tending to Ausgazur
passages.text:
You made it! 

<She looks at the outstretched hand of the earthen next to her and sighs.>

I admit that I am quite disturbed by what I've found here. Your presence is a comfort.

passages.title: Foreign Fog
passages.text:
Pleasure to meet you, adventurer. I wonder if you might be willing to help me with some research?

I'm sure you've noticed the fog beasts that have recently started encroaching upon this area. 

People see them as a bad omen, they always seem to show up during periods of ecological imbalance. I disagree with this assertion. 

Still as an expert in all vapor-based magics, I've been hired to find out where they're coming from so they can be cut off at the source.

passages.title: Foreign Fog
passages.text: Have you collected the fog samples?

passages.title: Foreign Fog
passages.text: Excellent! I'll start evaluating these samples right away.

passages.title: Fog Tags
passages.text:
While I analyze these fog samples, I have another task for you.

My employers have asked me to figure out where these fog beasts are coming from. I've developed these trackers. If you could, please attach them to an assortment of fog beasts. 

You'll have to get close, so... be careful. Hopefully they don't mind it too much!

passages.title: Fog Tags
passages.text: Have you attached all the trackers?

passages.title: Fog Tags
passages.text: You've attached the trackers? Perfect! Did they attack you? No? Interesting... This is all so interesting...

passages.title: Unnatural Predators
passages.text:
It would be no use tagging fog beasts to study if they all were to die, would it? 

Could you clear out some of the aggressive deepflayers that have flocked to feast on the fog beasts?

They'll ruin my data if left unchecked, I'm sure of it.

passages.title: Unnatural Predators
passages.text: Have you taken out the deepflayers?

passages.title: Unnatural Predators
passages.text:
Thank you. A researcher's duty is  to not interfere with nature, but... I only have so many trackers. 

I can't risk losing them to a bored, murderous deepflayer. No other reasons certainty. Hehe!

passages.title: Fog Follower
passages.text:
With the trackers attached, we should be able to find out where the fog beasts are coming from. The trackers leave a residue in the air. It's invisible to the naked eye, but I can use the mists to reveal it in places where there's a high enough concentration.

Theoretically, this should lead us to the places they most frequent. Maybe a nest! That I'll then have to report to my employer... hm.

Anyway. Let's see what we can find.

passages.title: Fog Follower
passages.text: I know we'll be able to find them. Let's keep looking!

passages.title: Fog Follower
passages.text:
Wow. I mean, wow! We learned so much in so little time! But now, I'm supposed to report this to people who want them gone?

I think people are wrong about the fog beasts. They don't attack unless threatened. And even when we entered their nest, they teleported us away safely. 

We haven't even had time to talk about the fact that they can do that kind of magic! Amazing!

passages.title: Sporadic Growth
passages.text:
Fungal growths are still spreading unchecked from the nearby Mycomancers' cavern. The latest surge has sent all my recruits fleeing in fear.

I urgently need your skills in eliminating one troublesome fungal growth.

Take my Patrol Torch and eradicate Gloomsprout and the surrounding growths that sprouts from it. The torch should handle the smaller stuff, but Gloomsprout will require a more direct approach

passages.title: Sporadic Growth
passages.text: Have you eliminated the threat?

passages.title: Sporadic Growth
passages.text: Excellent work, have you considered the possibility of a career in the Arathi Military?

passages.title: Let's Not Worry Her
passages.text:
Right, we better get back to Haimaz before she gets suspicious.

Please, don't tell her about any of this. Her duty is to guide and guard me in my role as compiler. 

If she knew I was planning to leave... I don't know what she would do.

passages.title: Let's Not Worry Her
passages.text: Thank you for bringing him back. He always acts strange when we come to Shadowvein Point, but he seems more out of sorts than usual.

passages.title: Lizard Looters
passages.text:
Despite the punishment of our posting here, life isn't entirely unpleasant. Captain Lancekat left us a generous supply of provisions. 

Well, at least she did until recently. A sizable lizard has made off with our camp supplies!

Could you recover our camp supplies and deal with the pilfering thief?

passages.title: Lizard Looters
passages.text: Did you find the supplies?

passages.title: Lizard Looters
passages.text: Fine work, we'll drink to your success as we feast on these supplies.

passages.title: Tenir and the Order of Night
passages.text: <A script for an epic stage play. Stage Manager Huberta on the Isle of Dorn may have interest in this.>

passages.title: Tenir and the Order of Night
passages.text: Very interesting, I will add this to my collection of unread submissions.

passages.title: To Mourning Rise
passages.text:
Greetings, outlander. My name is Urtago, and I am Caretaker Korgran's apprentice at the Mourning Rise memorial site.

The mischievous Candlelit Kobolds have overrun Mourning Rise, and we seek assistance. Would you meet me at Fallside Outpost? It is just to the north of here. I will be able to tell you more once you arrive.

passages.title: To Mourning Rise
passages.text: You are here! Thank you for coming.

passages.title: Sticks and Bones
passages.text:
While the krolusks like to attack from beneath, the Rumbling Waste also plays host to a predator who prefers to swoop down from above. Deepsflayers have built nests on the peaks and ridges around the Waste. 

Destroy their nests and show them that the Waste is no welcoming home.

passages.title: Sticks and Bones
passages.text: Let's show those overgrown bats that the Wastes is no home for them!

passages.title: Sticks and Bones
passages.text: I could see the smoke from here! Good job! That ought to make those wretched things look for a new place to perch.

passages.title: Azj-Kahet's Next Top Dyemaster
passages.text:
Ren'khat and the Overspinner are fighting pincer-and-claw. Inside the spinneret. With no witnesses.

We have a unique opportunity here. If they took one another out... well, with Antourix's favorites dispatched and the whole of Rak-Ahat in disarray, the next best authority would be the caravan coordinator. Me.

I don't love being in the spotlight, but it would be very beneficial to our secret-smuggling operation if those two didn't make it out of the dyeworks.

passages.title: Azj-Kahet's Next Top Dyemaster
passages.text: What a relief not to hear those two bickering anymore...

passages.title: Azj-Kahet's Next Top Dyemaster
passages.text:
The sheer scandal will have the record-keepers in the City of Threads busy for months.

And I'll make sure they don't look too closely at how it happened.

passages.title: Subterfuge in Silk
passages.text:
I'm expecting a shipment of silk. That it hasn't arrived worries me.

Most silk in Azj-Kahet, from the finest veils to the strongest warsilk, comes from Rak-Ahat. It makes the place a convenient nexus of information.
