passages.title: Strong Heart
passages.text:
The years passed, and Jeytha felt her time coming. She'd lived a long life, full of struggles but still happy. But as Jeytha reached the end of her days, dat sly old fox appeared. 

"Wait!" he said. "You can't go yet!"

Now what does that fox want? Go talk to him and find out!

passages.title: Strong Heart
passages.text: The sly fox ran off, grateful for Jeytha's boon. And Jeytha left her old bones a little after that--quieter, but just as content.

passages.title: Data Decryption Disaster
passages.text:
To understand the Hal'hadar's intentions with this world, we will need to secure information.

Knowing how they operate, they've restricted their data consoles with security measures in place.

<Y'mera smiles as she hands you a rune-carved crystal.>

This decrypter will automatically navigate their security. If you choose, you can engage the manual option to hasten the protocol.

Just remember to ignore any security warnings. My device can and will bypass it.

passages.title: Data Decryption Disaster
passages.text:
In the past, the Hal'hadar never stayed in one location for long, leaving whatever world they scavenged from just as quickly as they arrived.

For whatever reason, their intent with this world appears to be different.

passages.title: Data Decryption Disaster
passages.text:
One moment, there is much to glean from this data...

<Y'mera murmurs under her breath as she works.>

Interesting. They found a tomb of some kind under the swamp and...

Oh, what's this? Intercepted transcripts!

It seems Leth'ir's attacks on Azeroth were unsanctioned. Hal'hadar leadership is not pleased.

This information is most useful, <name>.

Good work.

passages.title: Hal'hadon't You Dare!
passages.text:
Y'mera's plan to intercept their data consoles will no doubt trigger heightened security protocols.

Normally, no-contact reconnaissance would be advised in this situation, but I think sowing chaos will be more beneficial.

The Hal'hadar won't be aware of their stolen data if their entire manaforge is under attack.

Dispatch any Hal'hadar agents you find.

passages.title: Hal'hadon't You Dare!
passages.text:
For every Hal'hadar slain, paranoia grows like a sickness through their ranks.

When distrust and fear is all that remains, their structure weakens and their operation falls.

My scouts will take advantage of the chaos you have created.

Good work, <name>.

passages.title: Conductive Crystals
passages.text:
<The glowing rune-marked crystal atop the Hal'hadar's device seems to be siphoning arcane spores out of the air.

Although you're not quite sure what the device is, you get the feeling the crystal isn't quite ethereal in origin.

Y'mera would definitely be interested in examining some of these crystals.>

passages.title: Conductive Crystals
passages.text: Yes, friend? What is it?

passages.title: Conductive Crystals
passages.text:
How fascinating!

My understanding of draenic might be a bit rusty but I believe these markings along the crystals matrices suggest they are used as a type of self-powered battery!

It seems the Hal'hadar are leveraging new ways to siphon arcane energy from this world!

But where did they get these crystals, I wonder?

Curious find!

passages.title: Technological Transference
passages.text:
The Hal'hadar are notorious for looting and stealing technology from any world they descend upon.

Thanks to the intel you helped retrieve, we know they are using the manaforge east of us to experiment on whatever salvage they found.

Take this translocator with you and mark anything that doesn't resemble ethereal technology.

I will transport it back here for further study.

passages.title: Technological Transference
passages.text:
I expected they found Legion or maybe Lightforged technology, but not draenei!

The vigilant appears to be severely damaged... its construct core entirely removed.

And the defense crystal is shattered beyond repair.

Did they find this here on Naigtal? Why bring it here otherwise?

There must be more to this. I will delve deeper into the data you found.

passages.title: The Node Knows
passages.text:
The manaforge to the east serves as both a research site and military compound, making it a valuable target.

Much of their research, including holoprint schematics, lays around the forge.

The Hal'hadar stationed here also carry nodes containing experimental and logistical data.

Take advantage of this accessible intel and bring back what you can find.

passages.title: The Node Knows
passages.text:
Sometimes effective reconnaissance requires careful planning and stealth. Other times, sudden ambushes and unleashed chaos are more effective.

I would know. I wrote the Lightveil Manifest, after all.

passages.title: The Node Knows
passages.text:
<Tala'saan's brow furrows in disbelief as he examines the holoprints.>

The crypt they found was built by... draenei?

This explains where the ethereals got the crystal conductors you found.

But how does it relate to this "Nullframe" they are building?

Our warframes aren't exactly compatible with standard crystal technology.

Perhaps Y'mera will find the answers in these data-nodes.

passages.title: Malfunctioning Nullframe
passages.text:
<From the runic communicator, you see a projection of a winged mechanical suit piloted by an ethereal. A voice emits from the device:

"Nullframe Soul-Fuse unsuccessful. Deployment from the Nexus Port halted. Troubleshooting in progress."

Whatever weapon the Hal'hadar created seems to be malfunctioning at the Transit Hub.

Intercepting and translocating the weapon back to Y'mera would deprive the ethereals of another weapon.>

passages.title: Malfunctioning Nullframe
passages.text: What have you found, <name>?

passages.title: Malfunctioning Nullframe
passages.text:
The state of this Nullframe is gravely concerning.

With the judgment core torn from its mainframe, there is no way to control the mech...

The Hal'hadar must be trying another means of piloting their twisted creation.

Veraan and Kifaan are more familiar with ethereal technomancy.

While they take a closer look, I will scour what data banks we've gathered.

passages.title: Soul Lattice Revealed
passages.text:
It took some work, but we've cracked their ciphers.

The Hal'hadar seek to power their Nullframes using draenei vigilant technology.

The "Soul Lattice" is a heart for the Nullframe using a vigilant's core.

With it, they can bind their unwrapped energy into the core and wear the frame like armor.

The Hal'hadar must not succeed in finishing this prototype.

Y'mera is planning the next move. Speak with her.

passages.title: Soul Lattice Revealed
passages.text:
Riftblade Maella agrees that the Hal'hadar in the crypt must be stopped.

It may not be the crux of their operation here on Naigtal, but it is not a threat we can ignore.

passages.title: Soul Lattice Revealed
passages.text:
Y'mera's data suggests the tomb is heavily congested with Hal'hadar.

While the rest of our forces rout the ethereals around the island, we'll opt for a more subtle approach.

Allari the Souleater has been monitoring the north coast and will join our infiltration into the crypt.

The irony of her title in such a place is not lost on me.

passages.title: Cryptside Rendezvous
passages.text:
The tomb is called Vilaldoun. It means "island of the restful." Its entrance lies on the northern coast.

We know the Hal'hadar have established an extraction site outside the crypt, harvesting the local flora there to fuel their research.

As you approach, you will be met with heavy resistance.

Cut a path through their ranks while we establish a footing inside and meet us within.

passages.title: Cryptside Rendezvous
passages.text: For a bunch of scavengers, these ethereals are far more provocative than I expected. It will make killing them all the more satisfying.

passages.title: Cryptside Rendezvous
passages.text:
I won't say I wasn't half tempted to join you up there, but someone's got to watch Y'mera's back.

Tala'saan's gone ahead to find the architect behind this operation.

We've managed to secure our position here in the stairwell, blocking any Hal'hadar who try to follow.

That leaves you to cut through this defiled place.

passages.title: Cages of the Soul
passages.text:
Without the tomb's defenses, the souls of the dead were easy targets for the Hal'hadar.

The ethereals intend to use the spirits to fuel the Soul Lattices for the Nullframe.

We must not let that happen.

Take my scepter and use it to repair the defense wards and shatter the energy cages binding the dead.

Once you've finished, regroup with Tala'saan in the lower chambers.

passages.title: Cages of the Soul
passages.text: We cannot allow the spirits of our dead kin to be harvested by these monsters.

passages.title: Cages of the Soul
passages.text:
I cannot help but wonder how long have these draenei been buried here...

How many cycles have gone by since this small corner of draenei civilization faded.

Was it the Legion who awoke them into unrest years ago? Or did the Hal'hadar's plundering disturb them?

All that matters now is that they return to their rest.

The wards will ensure they are not disturbed again.

passages.title: Mementos of the Dead
passages.text:
Defiling tombs... harnessing innocent souls as fuel...

The Hal'hadar are no better than demons.

If left unchecked, the ethereals will pilfer every grave and altar down here.

I may bear the title of "Souleater," but it doesn't mean I can't honor the dead in this forgotten place.

Recover the tributes the ethereals have stolen. Bring them to Tala'saan in the lower chamber.

passages.title: Mementos of the Dead
passages.text:
<Tala'saan appears quite calm, his armor flecked with arcane smatterings of the ethereals he slew.>

What did you find?

passages.title: Mementos of the Dead
passages.text:
<Tala'saan is silent for a moment as he examines the mementos you recovered.>

Allari asked you to recover these?

And here I was assuming her investment in our mission was simply an excuse to slaughter ethereals.

Thank you, <name>.

I will see to it these mementos are laid to rest in a more secure location.

passages.title: The Soul Architect
passages.text:
The architect leading their operation has found a single vigilant with an intact construct core.

The other vigilants in this chamber appear to be depleted.

If she succeeds in creating the Soul Lattice, the Hal'hadar will possess the means to turn our warframes into new armored bodies for their soldiers.

We must stop her now and recover the Soul Lattice prototype.

passages.title: The Soul Architect
passages.text: If the Hal'hadar succeed in forging a Soul Lattice, then they may possess the means to use our technology against us.

passages.title: The Soul Architect
passages.text:
It is done and yet...

<Tala'saan trails off for a moment as he thinks, his brow furrowed.>

The Soul Lattice may be broken, but there is something we are still missing.

The vigilants she took were vacant, their cores depleted of the souls that inhabited them.

What "true key" did she seek if not their construct cores? Why would she take empty husks?

passages.title: Cryptic Departure
passages.text:
Although she escaped, we have denied the architect her prototype... for now.

This Soul Lattice is fractured, but the core within still hums with a faint energy.

Perhaps this vigilant's soul yet remains...

If we hurry, perhaps Veraan and her brother can help stabilize the damage to preserve it.

I will regroup with Y'mera and Allari and meet you back at camp.

passages.title: Cryptic Departure
passages.text:
<Veraan examines the Soul Lattice.>

I am no expert on the Hal'hadar's work but even I can tell the damage here is significant.

At this rate, the vigilant core won't remain intact for much longer.

If Kifaan and I can unravel the lattice carefully, maybe we can pry the core loose.

If we're extra careful, perhaps we can preserve the lattice as well.

I make no promises, <name>.

passages.title: Ancient Curiosity: Combat
passages.text: <You hold the curio and discover a shimmering glow emanating from it. This looks important.>

passages.title: Ancient Curiosity: Utility
passages.text: <You hold the curio and discover a shimmering glow emanating from it. This looks important.>

passages.title: Equipment Seminar
passages.text:
Welcome back, <name>! I've continued my collaboration with the artisans here in Silvermoon. Their techniques have only grown more refined. Infusing equipment with the essence of the dawn is no longer just theory, it's becoming an art form.

I'm eager to resume our work together. Bring me another piece of Adventurer equipment, and we'll see how these improved methods hold up in practice.

Plenty of people are always in need of a capable hand. Help them, and they'll reward you accordingly.

passages.title: Equipment Seminar
passages.text: With my improved methods, I can make this far better. All we need left are the reagents.

passages.title: Upgrade Practicum
passages.text:
Cuzolth and I have pushed our craft further than ever, allowing us to imbue your gear with greater power.

To unlock its full potential, we'll need Mistcrests. They're drawn from trials of all kinds--greater dangers yield stronger crests, though even Adventurer Mistcrests carry a spark of that power.

Bring me fifty Adventurer Mistcrests, <name>. Let's see what your equipment is truly capable of.

passages.title: Upgrade Practicum
passages.text: If Adventurer Mistcrests prove elusive, turn your gaze to the hidden corners of the forbidden island that the Amani are currently exploring. Their efforts may yield exactly the Mistcrests we seek.

passages.title: Upgrade Practicum
passages.text:
Fantastic! Just what I was hoping for.

You're growing stronger with each step... which is, of course, my primary concern. My research simply benefits alongside it. Naturally.

passages.title: Veteran Symposium
passages.text:
There is a lot more power where that came from!

Upgrades scale with strength. Higher quality items can reach higher heights of power. For this step, I'll need Veteran equipment along with some Veteran Mistcrests.

Once you bring them, Cuzolth and I can continue making the enhancements.

passages.title: Veteran Symposium
passages.text: Completing a Heroic dungeon or a challenging weekly activity with the Amani expedition should grant you the Veteran equipment you seek. Taking part in their efforts should also get us those Veteran Mistcrests!

passages.title: Veteran Symposium
passages.text:
Good work, you're a natural at this!

The process always stays the same: bring us the item along with the appropriate crests, and Cuzolth will handle the upgrade.

passages.title: Patrolling the Temple
passages.text:
No sense standin' around. You've got a strong back and sharp eyes--best put them to use. We can't afford to let de serpents gain a single inch. 

Patrol de temple. You see someone who needs help? You help them. You find someone beyond saving? Make sure de fiends dat hurt them pay.

passages.title: Patrolling the Temple
passages.text: Fine work. If I had a hundred more death knights like you we'd have de temple cleared out in a week.

passages.title: Bounty of the Cursed
passages.text: Dis temple holds many secrets, adventurer. Ancient power, just waitin' for someone to take it. De Soulcoilers might be dead, but their power remains. Find their caches and bring me whatever you find.

passages.title: Bounty of the Cursed
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Bounty of the Cursed
passages.text: We'll use de Soulcoilers' own works to purge dem.

passages.title: Relentless Strikes
passages.text:
Some say de forces of Ula'tek are endless--dat we can never kill them all.

<Socho grins.>

But I like a challenge. How 'bout you? Strike de enemy hard, and we'll see how endless dey are.

passages.title: Relentless Strikes
passages.text: Take de fight to de enemy. We won't give dem a second of rest.

passages.title: Relentless Strikes
passages.text: Dis isn't your first war, is it? De serpents gonna learn to fear you before dis is done.

passages.title: Decisive Incursions
passages.text:
De strikes are de first step. We cannot let de enemy recover. First we batter them, soften 'em up. Then, we hit dem hard and fast with everything we've got. 

We don't have de forces for a longer battle. When de time comes for de incursion, you'd best be ready.

Gather your allies. De enemy is mighty.

passages.title: Decisive Incursions
passages.text: Now dat was a battle worthy of de old songs! I can see why Zul'jarra likes you.

passages.title: From Whence it Came
passages.text: Can you feel it? Old things lurk in de temple, just waitin' to rise once again. Dey are drawn by the sounds of battle, eager to visit their violence upon you. Find one of these ancient foes and ensure it does not rise again.

passages.title: From Whence it Came
passages.text: Can you feel it? De violence just waitin' to spill over?

passages.title: From Whence it Came
passages.text: Keep your blades sharp. De temple never sleeps for long.

passages.title: Essence of Malice
passages.text:
I'm in need of venom, pure and potent. De venom dat wells up through de ground is too diluted--fouled with other things. You need to find a font of de profane stuff.

Search de depths of de vaults. Dat's where de true venom will be found.

passages.title: Essence of Malice
passages.text: Well, do you have it?

passages.title: Essence of Malice
passages.text:
<Er'inye takes the vial, a wicked smile playing across her face.>

Oh, you've done well. Dis is even more than I was hopin' for.

passages.title: Mistcrest Capstone
passages.text:
Crests aren't fixed in form, you can transmute them between tiers.

If you're holding crests beyond what your current gear can use, I can refine them into lower tiers. And once your equipment advances, we can reverse the process and elevate lesser crests into greater ones.

Let's start with a simple exercise. Bring me those Veteran Mistcrests, and I'll convert them into Adventurer Mistcrests.

passages.title: Mistcrest Capstone
passages.text: If you lose those Veteran Mistcrests, you can find more from powerful creatures near the Amani Expedition. I've heard there's quite a variety of them!

passages.title: Mistcrest Capstone
passages.text:
Amazing work!

Remember: transmutation upward is only possible once a crest has outlived its usefulness to your gear, and it comes at a considerable cost.

Thank you for your assistance, <name>.

passages.title: Veterans of the Great Dark
passages.text:
When the Hal'hadar attacked, we quickly learned about their history with the Army of the Light.

Commander Tala'saan has been providing us information on these ethereals. His soldiers stand ready to join our cause.

I've requested their expertise in establishing a forward camp for our mission.

Aid them in their preparations and inform the commander we mobilize soon.

passages.title: Veterans of the Great Dark
passages.text:
I'll admit, after the events of the Voidspire, I remain cautious about relying on allies so... dedicated to the Light.

But personal reservations aside, I cannot deny their expertise in fighting the void and the Hal'hadar.

passages.title: Veterans of the Great Dark
passages.text:
Tala'saan did forewarn me only a few Lightforged could be spared. The attack on the Voidspire left their forces decimated.

Many wounded, many more slain or missing.

Any support we can muster from the Army of the Light will go a long way in this operation.

passages.title: [DNT]
To the Voidstorm and Beyond!
passages.text:
It may not seem like many, but the allies we've secured will have to be enough.

It's time we move out.

Our forces are gathering at the Howling Ridge. The energies of the Voidstorm will allow us to open the way to these worlds.

I will meet you there. There is something here I still require for our mission.

passages.title: To the Voidstorm and Beyond!
passages.text: Our enemies will not be expecting our assault. We must strike fast and true.

passages.title: To the Voidstorm and Beyond!
passages.text:
This may be an unusual coalition of allies, but each one leverages expertise we can use against our enemies.

Even Decimus cannot deny that.

I've secured the last component we need, the Cynosure of Twilight, to open the rift to where these ethereals and void forces operate from.

Are you ready, <name>?

passages.title: The Nexus-Captain (Heroic)
Imperator Pertinax (Heroic)
Showdown on Val
passages.text:
Our enemy's hold on Val may be strong, but it is not unbreakable.

For every monstrosity we cut down, we deny them another soldier to use against our world.

Venture out into the frozen landscape and lay waste to their strongholds.

Show them no mercy, <name>.

passages.title: Showdown on Val
passages.text: Something to report?

passages.title: Showdown on Val
passages.text:
By disrupting the domanaar's operation, you divert their attention away from Azeroth.

You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Showdown on Val (Heroic)
passages.text:
Our enemy's hold on Val may be strong, but it is not unbreakable.

For every monstrosity we cut down, we deny them another soldier to use against our world.

Venture out into the frozen landscape and lay waste to their strongholds.

Show them no mercy, <name>.

You have my thanks, <name>.

Show them no mercy, <name>.

You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Showdown on Naigtal
passages.text:
Now this is quite a strange world, isn't it?

The Hal'hadar must have found something of note.

The stench of forges indicates they are plundering the riches and resources this remote rock has to offer.

If you can disrupt the operations here, you can buy your precious world a moment of respite.

Do what you do best, my little monster.

passages.title: Showdown on Naigtal
passages.text: I trust you bring tales of wanton destruction to share with me?

passages.title: Showdown on Naigtal
passages.text:
My, you have been quite the busy engine of chaos, haven't you?

I always delight in your dramatic tales of... heroism. Take a moment to bask in the glow of the destruction you created.

Don't wander too far now. We are not quite done with this little fungal world.

passages.title: Showdown on Naigtal (Heroic)
passages.text:

The stench of forges indicates they are plundering the riches and resources this remote rock has to offer.

If you can disrupt the operations here, you can buy your precious world a moment of respite.

Do what you do best, my little monster.

Don't wander too far now. We are not quite done with this little fungal world.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Val
passages.text:
The mysterious world of Val has been made accessible to us with a host of new creatures present.

Go and see what you can find out about them.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Val
passages.text: There's still more to do.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Val
passages.text: That provides some answers, many thanks.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Naigtal
passages.text:
The mysterious world of Naigtal has been made accessible to us with a host of new creatures present.

Go and see what you can find out about this world and what the ethereals are up to.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Naigtal
passages.text: There's still more to do.

passages.title: Sparks of War: Naigtal
passages.text: That provides some answers, many thanks.

passages.title: Midnight: Offworld Showdowns
passages.text:
Our effort to thwart the Void Assaults in Eversong and Zul'Aman have seen much success, but if we do not find a way to stop our aggressors from coming to our lands, they will bleed us until we can no longer stand.

Riftblade Maella has recently discovered the location of two of our enemies' bases. She seeks to take the fight to them. Will you aid her strike team?

Your efforts will not go unnoticed in these dark times!

passages.title: Midnight: Offworld Showdowns
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. You have taken the fight to the doorstep of our enemies. With your efforts, we hope to reduce one enemy who threatens our world.

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 1 of 3
passages.text:
After you reported thinning out their ranks I got to thinking. 

What do they use to recruit members? Are they just as fanatical as their leaders?

I wonder if we can break their will to fight by destroying a greater number of their ranks. I fear it will take more than one example to know for sure.

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 1 of 3
passages.text:
The second ritual was just as protected as the first?

Well, I cannot say I am surprised. Our own people wouldn't be easily deterred and well their leaders are very persuasive. We also have set back the ambitions of these groups again and again.

I will study what you have brought me and have a new assignment for you soon.

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 2 of 3
passages.text:
I have your next assignment, <race>. I need you to study the resilience of these malevolent boons and their dark obelisks.

They focus magic so well and the variety of boons is interesting. I need more data though.

When you disrupt the next ritual site I need you to do so with these malevolent boons present.

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 2 of 3
passages.text: What did you discover?

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 2 of 3
passages.text:
This time consistency is in our favor. Well my favor at least. 

Your report fills in a few gaps I had in understanding how the obelisks interact and connect with their forces.

Thank you again, I will prepare a new lesson for you.

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 3 of 3
passages.text:
I think I am on the brink of a big discovery. These latest rituals involve a magic I had not previously heard of in the form of powerful embers that use the energy of their own forces to bolster their leader.

If you disrupt these rituals and report your findings to me, I might be able to put this magic to use for us. Do not look at me that way. On my own demon minions of course. Did you think I meant troops like you?

We are much too early for trials like that. Report back with your findings!

passages.title: Ritual Site Studies: Week 3 of 3
passages.text:
Hmm... your notes are not as detailed as I would like. I do wish you had left more of them active when you took on their leader...

I guess that may have resulted in your death and loss of the data so I will make due. This is promising. 

Oh, you are still here. Yes, I promised you a reward for helping me with this line of inquiry.

I wonder, if we were to study these in specific combinations... well that is for another time.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 4 of 6
passages.text:
I had an idea right after you left. 

We have thinned out their ranks, we have also seen that they can summon additional reinforcements.

I want to test the limits of their reserves.

If you take on this set of challenges, I promise you another key for the vault.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 4 of 6
passages.text:
This is starting to bear fruit. While they did maintain their troop numbers in your latest attempts to disrupt the ritual they slowed by just a few seconds on that last alarm portal.

<race>, we just have to keep up the pressure. They will break soon I am sure. We must look into these obelisks next.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 5 of 6
passages.text:
Now that we have tested their troop reserves, our focus will be the dark obelisks and these boons they give.

This requires close scrutiny and will surely entail you facing increased patrols while you explore the site. Not too difficult for someone like yourself.

Just avoid them... or deal with them if you must.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 5 of 6
passages.text:
This is good, the dark obelisks are more resilient than I thought. You look surprised again. Of course this is good news I think I almost have learned enough to fashion something like them myself.

Now, can't you see how much of a boon this would be? It's not always about denying or destroying the enemies assets. Often it is learning how to use their tools against them... or other threats.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 6 of 6
passages.text:
Welcome back my star pupil. I have one last assignment for you and this one will be a challenge.

These embers that they use in these rituals. I have not had any success in replicating them or finding a way to counter them.

I have one last idea I want you to try. You reported seeing magical manifestations of caster spirits. I have a theory that with these two challenges present there might be a way for them to cancel each other out.

passages.title: Advanced Ritual Site Studies: Week 6 of 6
passages.text:
It did not work? Well that is disappointing. It was worth a chance, that is something you will learn if you continue to study rituals. Sometimes you just have to try things.

At times it will amount to nothing, other times it can let you summon a giant demon to smite your foes. I don't recommend the latter for you. It probably wouldn't go well for you or your foe.

Well that is all I have need of from you. Take the key and my thanks!

passages.title: Bouncy Mushrooms
passages.text:
Hello! Here's a trick to help you bounce on the purple mushrooms around here. You'll need it, because...

I want some canopy specimens from the sporerays above us. Bounce up there, get some specimens, then come back down and I'll teach you how to ALWAYS bounce on those mushrooms.

passages.title: Bouncy Mushrooms
passages.text: I need those specimens. Bounce on the mushrooms and look for Sporerays.

passages.title: Bouncy Mushrooms
passages.text: Thank you. I'll put these to good use. Now you can jump on those mushrooms all the time.

passages.title: Aerospores
passages.text:
Now, practice using aerospores. They're up there too if you know where to look. Use them to shoot through the air!

You'll need to bounce on mushrooms to get up to the spores and see them. Once you're up there, pass through some aerospores and find out what they do!

passages.title: Aerospores
passages.text:
Well done. You did the hard part, now let me tell you the trick to it.

<He tells you the trick to using aerospores.>

passages.title: Sporefall: Rotmire
passages.text:
Need help! End of Harandar! End of world!

Spore Storm making something new for Grudge Pit, but too much. Too much! Can't control. Will break free! Destroy pit. Destroy us all!

Must go to Sporefall, destroy Rotmire before they lose control!

For Harandar! For Azeroth! For Grudge Pit!

passages.title: Sporefall: Rotmire
passages.text:
You save us all. Fungaria! Harandar! World! Grudge Pit!

But world, mostly world.

passages.title: Calling All Combatants!
passages.text:
<You read a nearby advertisement...>

Run, don't walk!

The Artisan's Consortium has teamed up with local Silvermoon artisans in Falconwing Square to offer a new selection of heraldries and crafted equipment. These are certified for use in arenas and battlegrounds, guaranteed!

Head on down and look for Mirvedon to receive your free sample today.

Act now while supplies last! Terms and conditions apply.

-Aisha

passages.title: Calling All Combatants!
passages.text:
<Mirvedon clears his throat.>

Take these heraldries straight over to the Crafting Order station to get a custom piece. Anything you make with these will keep you safe while crossing swords in the battlegrounds. If you ever want more heraldries I've got what you need.

For a price this time, of course.

passages.title: Sparks of War: The Coiled Isle
passages.text:
There's unknown danger out in the Coiled Isle.

Get out there and clear things up!

passages.title: Sparks of War: The Coiled Isle
passages.text: Well, get on then!

passages.title: Sparks of War: The Coiled Isle
passages.text: Many thanks for clearing things out.

passages.title: Exterior Manaforge Translocator
passages.text:
Maneuvering through this spore-infested rock is quickly becoming a chore, I'm sure you would agree.

Thankfully, I've figured out a way to make use of the existing Manaforge Translocator network that was so thoughtfully built prior to our arrival.

I can show you how to "activate" them for our use. You can start with the one we... translocated to camp.

passages.title: Exterior Manaforge Translocator
passages.text: Have the Manaforge Translocators been activated?

passages.title: Exterior Manaforge Translocator
passages.text: Superb! Now we'll be able to navigate swiftly and unseen.

passages.title: The Grappler
passages.text: You have to try this Lightforge Hookshot! Here, take this loaner one. To learn the ropes, use it on some mushrooms and aerospores around here. Come back and I'll give you a Hookshot for keeps.

passages.title: The Grappler
passages.text: Get out there, <name>. Grapple onto those mushrooms and aerospores. And don't forget to have fun!

passages.title: The Grappler
passages.text: What did you think? Useful here, yes? Here's one for you to keep. Watch yourself out there!

passages.title: Accolades for the Umbral Contender
passages.text:
<name>, you continue to impress me with your martial prowess!

You've done such an incredible job defeating the forces of evil. I've got something from my coffers that I'd love to give you.

passages.title: Accolades for the Umbral Contender
passages.text:
You're incredible, <name>!

Please have this saddle as a token of my appreciation.

passages.title: Turn Back the Surge
passages.text:
De temple can no longer contain Ula'tek's wrath. De boldest of her brood are spilling out all over de isle! They'll destroy us all if we don't stem de tide of venom.

Fight dem wherever dey dare to show their ugly heads. Do not let dem get a foothold.

passages.title: Turn Back the Surge
passages.text: We must survive.

passages.title: Turn Back the Surge
passages.text:
Dat will keep them at bay... until the next surge, anyway.

<Zela regards you grimly.>

Don't let your guard down.

passages.title: Mixing Mysteries
passages.text:
You think you've got some potent ingredients for my stew, eh? We'll see what de spirits think.

Show me what you've brought and I'll throw it in de cauldron. De spirits will eat their fill, and if dey like it, you might get a reward.

Or a punishment, if dey hate it. So choose wisely!

passages.title: Mixing Mysteries
passages.text:
<The spirits have received your offering and grant you one in return.

Are they pleased? Are they angry? Are they feeling a little mischievous?

You will know soon enough.>

passages.title: Esoteric Ingredients
passages.text:
<These mundane materials have acquired a queer shine to them, almost as if you are noticing a power latent in them that you could not perceive before.

Must have something to do with all that corrosion you've been consuming.

You aren't sure how to unlock that latent power, but perhaps there is someone more familiar with the esoteric magic of the isle that could help.>

passages.title: Esoteric Ingredients
passages.text:
Oh yes. Dis is a big cauldron indeed.

I know exactly what to do with dis.

passages.title: Vilaldoun Valediction
passages.text:
<A brief glint sparkling in the shadows catches your eye.

As you pick up the object, the gem in its center flickers briefly, strange alien runes flashing across its surface.

For a moment, you see a flickering recorded projection of a male draenei mouthing silent words.

Y'mera will definitely be interested in this object.>

passages.title: Vilaldoun Valediction
passages.text:
You found this in the tomb?

This is a hologem--a draenei tool used for communication and storing information.

It looks to be nearly depleted of its power. The ethereals must've thought this to be some mere trinket.

I will see if I can energize it and access the information within.

Perhaps it will reveal more about those buried within Vilaldoun.

passages.title: Vanquish the Warmonger
passages.text:
Poor Impotus doesn't seem to believe we can seize control from his nefarious kin. He's tragically unimaginative.

We'll just need to show him an example of our combined strength. Slay that brute of a newcomer, Ignedus. I think his armor would look nice on our new savior.

Ignedus seems to be quite careful in showing his face, but clearly quick to anger. Get in there and make some noise, as you're so comfortable doing. I expect him to respond in kind.

passages.title: Vanquish the Warmonger
passages.text: You are a fool if you think Ignedus can be dealt with so swiftly.

passages.title: Vanquish the Warmonger
passages.text: You actually... I mean, of course you succeeded. Obviously, I would not choose the losing side.

passages.title: Depose the Deranged
passages.text:
Defeating Ignedus is impressive, I suppose, but it does not mean you're any closer to taking Val. Periculus won't let you meddle with his playthings.

He is an... eccentric one, to say the least, and dreadfully fascinated by you flesh-beings.

You'll likely find him in the darkest hole this world has to offer, carving open the livestock that Pertinax gathered.

He likes to toy with his prey, so I would advise caution.

passages.title: Depose the Deranged
passages.text: I will not take command of this world while Periculus is stalking about. He... disturbs me...

passages.title: Depose the Deranged
passages.text: So it is done? That's a relief for any living creature in the cosmos.

passages.title: Umbral Title Bout
passages.text:
Well then, it seems our goals are more aligned than before. You've impressed me. With Ignedus and Periculus dealt with, all that remains is my former associate.

You will find Gladius Reginax atop that high platform, observing her quarry. She already knows you're coming, so don't aim to surprise her. There's only one way up there for you anyway: through that portal in the Glacial Reservoir.

I will play my part and join you. A symbol of our... collaboration.

passages.title: Umbral Title Bout
passages.text: Just one more piece to play and Val will be ours.

passages.title: Umbral Title Bout
passages.text: Well, aren't you a devious creature. How does it feel to play with pawns of your own?

passages.title: Stargrim Revelations
passages.text:
We have a problem, <name>.

The hologem you found revealed much about our people's time on this world and who the vigilants were in life.

Who they were is not the problem, but rather the possessions they carried within their chassis.

Possessions now in the hands of the Soul Architect who, as far as my scouts can tell, has left Naigtal.

Archmage Y'mera will explain in greater detail.

passages.title: Stargrim Revelations
passages.text:
You, good. Friend of mine. Trust. For showing.

Wait here enough. Must go. Stop ethereal. Find--

<Tul'amar cuts herself off and looks past you. Someone's coming.>

passages.title: A Frigid Welcome to Val
passages.text:
Even with the element of surprise, we are at a disadvantage without allies.

Storming Pertinax's stronghold alone would be a death sentence.

Take this beacon Tala'saan gave us and return to our entry point.

I will meet you there and deliver my report to Maella.

Let us hope we have some sort of shelter awaiting us.

passages.title: A Frigid Welcome to Val
passages.text:
At least the cold didn't kill you.

Thanks to Y'mera, we have a more stable entry point into this frozen world.

Her beacon also connects back to Silvermoon, giving us a quick evacuation point should we need it.

With the surveillance beacons in place and our foothold established, we can get to work.

Welcome to Val, <name>.

passages.title: A Swampy Welcome to Naigtal
passages.text:
The Nexus-Captain is just over that hill, unaware of our arrival.

Attacking now would catch his army off guard... and likely result in our demise.

No matter what, we will need allies if we are to succeed.

Use this beacon to return to our invasion point.

By now, Y'mera has likely brought in the rest of our forces to support us.

Speak with Maella when you arrive.

passages.title: A Swampy Welcome to Naigtal
passages.text:
Glad to see the swamp didn't swallow you whole.

Y'mera's efforts have provided a more stable entry point into this world.

Her beacon also connects back to Silvermoon, allowing us a quick fallback point if needed.

With the surveillance beacons in place and our foothold established, we can get to work.

Welcome to Naigtal, <name>.

passages.title: A Shot at the Dark
passages.text:
Now that our trap is attuned, we just need to lure our prey out into the open.

I have strategically... dismantled... certain parts of the projection device I obtained. Impotus should have difficulty seeing and hearing you clearly.

Claim to be one of his allies and demand a meeting at once. We will hope his curiosity gets the better of him.

And then... 

<Leona holds up the void-infused gem, glances at it for a moment, then nods at you.>

passages.title: A Shot at the Dark
passages.text: I know we wished for a more docile dignitary, but must he be this... stale?

passages.title: More Disruptions: Val
passages.text:
We must not let up the pressure.

Even now they are rebuilding from our attacks.

Venture out again and show them no mercy!

passages.title: More Disruptions: Val
passages.text: Something to report?

passages.title: More Disruptions: Val
passages.text: I knew we could rely on you, <name>.

passages.title: More Disruptions: Val (Heroic)
passages.text:
We must not let up the pressure. Even now they are rebuilding from our attacks. 

Venture out again and again show them no mercy!

passages.title: More Disruptions: Val (Heroic)
passages.text: I knew I could count on you for this task, <name>.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Val
passages.text:
Our scouts have reported seeing dangerous elite creatures that are hampering our efforts. 

I need you to dispatch them so we can continue our primary objective.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Val
passages.text: I knew I could count on you for this task, <name>.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Val (Heroic)
passages.text:
Our scouts have reported seeing dangerous elite creatures that are hampering our efforts. 

I need you to dispatch them so we can continue our primary objective.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Val (Heroic)
passages.text: Something to report?

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Val (Heroic)
passages.text: I knew I could count on you for this task, <name>.

passages.title: More Disruption: Naigtal
passages.text:
The stench of their forges still lingers. This means they are rebuilding. 

You must keep at it if you hope to disrupt their operations enough to end their threat.

Now you can go. Wreak havoc.

passages.title: More Disruption: Naigtal
passages.text:
Oh, you are back. Was that explosion your doing?

It appears your efforts are taking a toll. The smell of smoke is replacing that wretched smell from their operation.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Naigtal
passages.text:
I hear your scouts talk of dangerous creatures and foes they have faced. 

It makes me wonder if you could defeat them? Why don't you go and try? It will certainly help your efforts here.

I hope to see you return mostly intact.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Naigtal
passages.text:
You did it? Oh, I am not surprised. You do seem to be rather lucky.

Maybe in time I will see enough evidence to attribute it to skill. 

Do you not have something else you should be about?

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Naigtal (Heroic)
passages.text:
I hear your scouts talk of dangerous creatures and foes they have faced. 

It makes me wonder if you could defeat them? Why don't you go and try? It will certainly help your efforts here.

I hope to see you return mostly intact.

passages.title: Dangerous Enemies: Naigtal (Heroic)
passages.text:
You did it? Oh, I am not surprised. You do seem to be rather lucky.

Maybe in time I will see enough evidence to attribute it to skill. 

Do you not have something else you should be about?

passages.title: More Disruption: Naigtal (Heroic)
passages.text:
The stench of their forges still lingers. This means they are rebuilding. 

You must keep at it if you hope to disrupt their operations enough to end their threat.

Now you can go. Wreak havoc.

passages.title: More Disruption: Naigtal (Heroic)
passages.text:
Oh, you are back. Was that explosion your doing?

It appears your efforts are taking a toll. The smell of smoke is replacing that wretched smell from their operation.

passages.title: Spoils of the Vaults
passages.text:
It takes de whole of our strength to keep de forces of Ula'tek from overwhelming de isle. Dat battle is waged inside the Vault of Ula'tek, against the endless tide of her children. Kill one, and two more will slither out of de venom.

Venture in, <name>, and lend your power to our weary fighters. Who knows? You may even find something valuable in dat ancient, cursed place.

passages.title: Spoils of the Vaults
passages.text: Careful not to fall in de rivers of venom.

passages.title: Spoils of the Vaults
passages.text: Dat should buy us some room to rally our strength.

passages.title: A Secondary Strike
passages.text:
We have struck a major blow against our enemies. Still, they continue their assaults.

Decimus and my riftwardens have targeted another world from which they launch these attacks.

The bulk of our forces have temporarily withdrawn to the Voidstorm so that we may begin our assault on this second world.

Our strike team awaits us at the Howling Ridge.

passages.title: A Secondary Strike
passages.text:
Our enemies have each established their strongholds on different worlds, forcing us to split our attention.

If we are to truly route their forces, we must strike at both and fortify our entry points.

Ready to breach another rift?

passages.title: Knocking Off the Top (Heroic)
passages.text:
Even the most ruthless of creatures falter when they see their greatest champions crumble to ash.

Remind our enemies here just how quickly their leaders fall!

Let them know just how unrelenting and vicious you monsters of Azeroth really are! Bring me the Void Commander's Emblems and I will reward you accordingly.

passages.title: Knocking Off the Top (Heroic)
passages.text: Are you done already?

passages.title: Knocking Off the Top (Heroic)
passages.text:
Diabolical as always. Your kind continue to remind me why I chose you to help me. 

As a reward, I have procured some items that you might find useful in our future endeavors. No need to tell your allies about this.

passages.title: Slithering Spoils
passages.text:
I've got good news and bad news.

Bad is that all those curios we dug up together? Melted.

Good news? I've found some very interesting new poisons to work with.

But let me explain what happened...

passages.title: Slithering Spoils
passages.text: What do you think?

passages.title: Slithering Spoils
passages.text: It was a rookie mistake, but it wasn't all for nothing.

passages.title: A Curated Gift
Counter-Curse Bounty
passages.text:
Every part of dis isle is cursed, <name>. When de curse of Ula'tek coalesces into a fight, dat is when it is most important to strike back. We need all de help we can get keeping it at bay.

You look strong... but you'll need better equipment if you want to stay alive.

Defeat the leader of one of dese surges, and then we can discuss a reward.

passages.title: Counter-Curse Bounty
passages.text: Careful not to fall in de rivers of venom.

passages.title: Counter-Curse Bounty
passages.text: Dat should teach dese snakes a lesson, but I can't imagine dey will take it to heart.

passages.title: Spirit Corrosion
passages.text: Our scouts found dis relic in one of da crypts. Maybe Er'inye knows what to do with it?

passages.title: Spirit Corrosion
passages.text: What's dat you got there?

passages.title: Spirit Corrosion
passages.text: Dis relic is old and powerful. I can transfer de corrosion to your spirit.

passages.title: More Spirit Corrosion
passages.text: One of those soulcoilers was carrying dis gem. You should show it to Er'inye.

passages.title: Seasonal Refresher: Midnight
passages.text:
Since the opening of the Coiling Isles, things have started to get interesting again in delves.

See if our dear hosts have anything they can spare for those of us actually risking our necks and check the Delver's Guide for any updates.

A quick refresher never hurt anyone.

passages.title: Seasonal Refresher: Midnight
passages.text: Good to go?

passages.title: Seasonal Refresher: Midnight
passages.text: Excellent, though there have been... developments since last we spoke.

passages.title: Call of the Bell
passages.text:
<Years beneath the waves should have erased its details, yet the bell remains remarkably well-preserved. Whatever purpose it once served, the runes carved into it were clearly meant to endure.

A sense of foreboding comes over you as you consider ringing it. Maybe not.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Fits Like a Glove
passages.text:
<These appear to be a large pair of hand bones, that someone has hollowed out and claimed to be gauntlets.

It's a good thing you're already wearing gauntlets, or you'd be tempted to try them on.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Fits Like a Glove
passages.text: I... suppose they could have aided the Quartermaster with hauling up fish?

passages.title: Tackled and Boxed
passages.text:
<An endless supply of fishing gear would be a dream for most anglers. The fact that this tacklebox screams whenever it is opened likely explains why it ended up at the bottom of the sea.

After spending enough time with it, the screams start to echo without needing to open it at all.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Tackled and Boxed
passages.text: Is this where all the screaming has been coming from? Birdie said it was the cannons.

passages.title: Something Smelly
passages.text:
<The inscription promises to not only attract spirits, but to whip them into a violent frenzy if enough is burned. That can't end well.

Still, it does smell nice.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Something Smelly
passages.text: Oh my, that smells curiously like Inktail's signature scent. She always had odd taste.

passages.title: Lightly Salted
passages.text:
<The pouch is unremarkable, but its history may not be. Ritual salts have long been used to call upon ancestors, spirits, and powers beyond the mortal world.

This salt is extra-salty, having been in the ocean. Perhaps that makes it extra-potent?

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Cursed Fishing 101
passages.text:
<Most fishing manuals concern themselves with bait, weather, and patience. This weathered tome boasts lessons on hexing one's fishing rivals and communing with the deep.

You sense you are wading into dangerous waters.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Rocky Shores
passages.text:
<This faceted ore hums with an unsettling energy. Whether it is valued more for its practical uses or its strange properties, you cannot say.

You feel compelled to lick it, though you know you shouldn't.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Just a Normal Knife
passages.text:
<This blade shows no signs of battle wear, only careful maintenance. Its purpose was clearly ceremonial, but for what ceremony?

The red gleam to the metal gives you a clue.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: Just a Normal Knife
passages.text: Oh dear. This most certainly belongs to the Captain.

passages.title: A Dash of Poison
passages.text:
<The glass is thick and reinforced, suggesting the contents were considered dangerous--or valuable. The verdant liquid within glimmers as it shifts in the vial.

You think you smell something acrid and noxious about it. But it could be that this whole isle smells acrid and noxious.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: A Dash of Poison
passages.text: How... mysterious! And green! This does seem like something Cook Leathertongue might hold onto.

passages.title: The Intended Way to Fish
passages.text:
<It's a spear. The fishing rod is a spear.

Sluggs probably knows something about this item.>

passages.title: The Intended Way to Fish
passages.text:
This is a spear. What else is there to mention?

I believe it belonged to Grenadier Birdie, not that she ever used it.

passages.title: Fangs for the Memories
passages.text:
That snake monstrosity was vicious, with venom potent enough to burn through stone.

We'll want to make sure we get our hands on the best gear we can before we think about taking it on.

I've got some ideas about turning that venom to our own ends, though, so we can hit the ground running.

passages.title: Fangs for the Memories
passages.text: Nicely done. It'll make a lovely pair of boots.

passages.title: A Bargain You Won't Refuse
passages.text:
<A voice hisses in your mind.>

Am I to be another victim in your pointless conquest? I wonder... will you skin me alive and boil me in a stew? Or simply leave me to rot on a pile of your forgotten excess?

What if I can offer you something... better? Something... delicious. The Children of Ula'tek are a blight on this world. On this we agree. Bring me proof of their demise.

passages.title: A Bargain You Won't Refuse
passages.text: You are a vicious one after all.

passages.title: A Bargain You Won't Refuse
passages.text: I was beginning to think you had reneged...

passages.title: Tailing the Tlhapi
passages.text:
Toxic Tlhapi. Nasty little fish.

Everything's wrong about them, from their big, buggy eyes to their sweet, succulent meat...

<Gills clears their throat.>

Not to mention the toxicity. The seas would be much better without them fouling things up.

passages.title: Tailing the Tlhapi
passages.text: Hmph. Should have asked for a lime, too.

passages.title: Tailing the Tlhapi
passages.text:
Oh yes, they'll do much better among the crew than they would in the open ocean.

I suspect Captain Tokka will be pleased.

passages.title: The Familiar Taste of Poison
passages.text:
Surely by now even you understand the threat Ula'tek poses, yes? Her wretched power oozes forth time and time again.

If I am to do my part, I will need proof of your devotion to our... agreement, shall we call it? When next her acolytes call forth their twisted mongrels, slay them and collect their remains.

passages.title: Culling the Killifish
passages.text:
Spotted Killifish. Grotesque little creatures.

The little demons swarm like insects, washing up on shores in such horrific numbers that it would take several meals to devour them all.

<Gills' belly burbles audibly.>

You can do your part by collecting some for me, ridding the waters of their foul presence.

passages.title: Culling the Killifish
passages.text: Hmph. Should have asked for a crack of fresh zandalari pepper.

passages.title: Culling the Killifish
passages.text:
Oh yes, these will be far more appreciated here than swimming about the seas.

I suspect Captain Tokka will be pleased.

passages.title: Tipping the Scaled
passages.text:
<The wretched things you gathered briefly wink out of existence, returning in the same breath as one object.>

Go on, take it. Carry it to the Vaults of Atal'Utek. Affix it to that dismal rod of yours and cast it into the fetid pools to draw out one of Ula'tek's pets. You do have the skill to fish anywhere, don't you?

passages.title: Dogging the Darters
passages.text:
Dirty Darters. Ghoulish little buggers.

The way they flit about the water is so unnerving, so disquieting, one can't help but imagine them darting right down one's gullet...

<Gills coughs rather loudly>

You can do your part by collecting some for me, ridding the waters of their foul presence.

passages.title: Dogging the Darters
passages.text: Hmph. Should have asked for some whale butter.

passages.title: Dogging the Darters
passages.text:
Oh yes, the crew will make quick work of these squirmy little devils.

I suspect Captain Tokka will be pleased.

passages.title: Corrosive Gifts: Corrosive Power
passages.text:
<You feel a change in the air as you take this ancient volume into your hands.

Though it prickles and burns your skin, your mind radiates with thoughts of the power it contains and the peril it represents.

You must know more.

There is only one place on the isle profane enough for this tome. In your mind's eye, you glimpse the Altar of Corrosion.>

passages.title: Corrosive Gifts: Corrosive Power
passages.text: You know not what you meddle with.

passages.title: Corrosive Gifts: Corrosive Power
passages.text:
So think you've found a way to de power of corrosion without ol' Er'inye, eh?

<Er'inye scoffs.>

Go on. See what it costs ya.

passages.title: The Singularity Anchor
passages.text:
Our sojourn to this world has brought the ren'dorei an even deeper understanding of the Void than before. The domanaar with whom we share a common enemy are almost strangely generous with their knowledge. I believe they want us to become as fearsome as they are.

There is a Singularity Anchor in Stormarion Citadel. I have learned how to draw upon some of its power to craft you a powerful item.

But first, we must ensure it does not fall into the hands of our enemies.

passages.title: The Singularity Anchor
passages.text: Have you defended the anchor from the encroaching void forces?

passages.title: The Singularity Anchor
passages.text: Well done, <name>.

passages.title: A Soiree to Remember
passages.text:
You seek an audience with Saltheril? And you're wearing... that? Excuse me for a moment while I laugh into my handkerchief.

<Caeris laughs lightly behind his handkerchief.>

Now, let me be professional. You are cordially invited to attend Saltheril's soiree.

Don't embarrass yourself, <name>. The best of Silvermoon are watching.

passages.title: A Soiree to Remember
passages.text: I half expected you to run back home in tears! I hope you had a stunning time.

passages.title: Seeking Legends
passages.text: Harandar hides wisdom in every annal of its history, <name>. You would do well to seek out its legends for yourself. I suspect you may learn something of this world and our places in it.

passages.title: Seeking Legends
passages.text: I wonder what it is that the stones showed you. I hope you found it enlightening, <name>. But remember: there is always more to learn.

passages.title: Glorious Abundance
passages.text:
De Loa of Abundance may not be one of de four great ones, but his worshippers are certainly de most devout.

Seek him out yaself. You can find him in northern Zul'Aman near Halazzi's Temple, but I also hear he's established harvest sites in Eversong Woods, Harandar, and even de land of Void through de gargantuan skymouth.

If nothing else, de rewards he grants are glorious--to de worthy, at least.

passages.title: Glorious Abundance
passages.text: Did you find de loa, hash'ura?

passages.title: Glorious Abundance
passages.text:
Heh! So ya finally met Dundun.

Even de smallest are some of de greatest among de loa!

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: One Coin Too Many
passages.text:
You don't look so good, <name>.

<As Abdumati examines you grimly, your heart starts pounding and your vision goes green. The weight of the coin in your pocket feels overwhelming.>

You found something out dere, huh? De vaults are full of treasure, most of it cursed.

I don't trust her, but dat spirit-witch you saw knows all de secrets of dis horrid place. If anyone can help, it's her.

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: One Coin Too Many
passages.text: When de corrosive coins start to weigh you down, come to me.

passages.title: The Protection of the Med'jai
passages.text:
<This amulet feels warm and smooth in your hand.

As you hold it, you feel relief from the weight of your corrosion, as if the amulet offers some protection from Ula'tek's curse.

Er'inye would likely be interested in studying it.>

passages.title: The Protection of the Med'jai
passages.text: Dis surprises me. Nothing in dese accursed vaults has surprised me in a long time.

passages.title: The Winds of Tok'jara
passages.text:
<As your hand closes around this fragile feather, a spectral wind echoes through the vaults.

With it, you feel the weight of your spirit's corrosion lift, as if you could simply spread your wings and fly out of this cursed place.

You can't, of course. But Er'inye might be interested in studying it.>

passages.title: The Winds of Tok'jara
passages.text: Hmph. Dere are powers lurking in dese vaults that even I am unaware of.

passages.title: The Watchful Gaze of Szarith
passages.text:
<Clutching the serpentine eyeball, you feel a new awareness creeping up the back of your neck.

The Eggs of Ula'tek. By the hundreds. You can sense their every twitching presence, waiting to burst into vile venom and more of her wretched spawn.

You wish you could toss it into the deepest crypt, but its power is undeniably potent. Er'inye would be interested in studying it.>

passages.title: The Watchful Gaze of Szarith
passages.text:
<Er'inye chuckles.>

You brought dis all de way here because you thought I would find it interesting? Well I do.

passages.title: The Luck of the Bound Spirit
passages.text:
<You hold a simple lynx's paw, worn by time and worry, that the spirit left as a parting gift.

Though it holds no magical properties of its own, it is swollen with the hopes and fears of every bound spirit that crossed its path in this miserable place.

The result is quite potent, if emotionally harrowing. Er'inye would likely be interested in studying it.>

passages.title: The Luck of the Bound Spirit
passages.text: Eugh. I do not like this one, though I cannot deny its power.

passages.title: Cracked Keystone
passages.text:
Fragmentary images of heroic deeds flash through your mind as you touch the stone, but they fade as fast as they arrive.

Perhaps performing a suitably impressive task will stabilize the stone's magic once more?

passages.title: In the Catalyst's Shadow
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! Good. Now that you've helped me amass such a wealth of resources, it's time for me to pursue other... interests.

What? You expected a more dramatic betrayal? Never!

Don't worry, adventurer, while I may be occupied elsewhere, I'll never tire of watching your adventures.

Adventures still bolstered by my gifts, of course. Many have shown interest, but I've only found one void elf... amusingly strange enough to mentor.

Orin Straylight is the name. You'll find him by the Catalyst in Silvermoon.

passages.title: In the Catalyst's Shadow
passages.text: Ah, so you spoke with Decimus? It looks like we're on our own now. Better get started.

passages.title: Prismatic Potential
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>. Our mutual friend explained everything to us. Don't worry, my shade and I took to Decimus' voidweaving like fish to water.

We had an idea. The Catalyst's transformative energies are immense and span the breadth of known elemental forces.

If I can learn to isolate the void from that spectrum of power, I could use it to weave Nebulous Voidcores just as Decimus did with the Voidforge.

We are no domanaar, though. We need practice.

passages.title: Prismatic Potential
passages.text: Do you have those Elementary Voidcore Shards?

passages.title: Prismatic Potential
passages.text: I hope it wasn't too difficult to come by these Elementary Voidcore Shards. Now that we have them, I can continue my research into the void potential of the Catalyst's power. This will take a while, so check back with me later.

passages.title: Trailing Xal'atath
passages.text:
We must not lose sight of our true goal here in Silvermoon, <name>: to bring Xal'atath to justice.

We all saw her void armies at the Sunwell. They were rushing downward, INTO the well, a thousand a minute. And now: silence.

Listen for their whispers, <class>. With any luck, we'll pick up on their trail again, and then we'll find Xal'atath... and perhaps even those that pursued her.

passages.title: Trailing Xal'atath
passages.text: Every whisper silenced is a step closer towards our true quarry.

passages.title: Trailing Xal'atath
passages.text:
Our hunt is far from over.

Keep your ears and eyes open, <name>.

passages.title: Cursed Keepsake
passages.text:
<A containment shield hums, wrapping tightly about the keepsake. The object projects an aura of sorrow and suffering.

According to the Last Architect, this keepsake is cursed, but it can be cleansed. One must simply fold their essence inside that of the object and remove the corruption from within. How dangerous could it be?>

passages.title: Cursed Keepsake
passages.text: To remove the corruption from the cursed keepsake directly, one must enter within and do battle with the echoes of the trauma haunting it. Once extracted, the corruption can be destroyed.

passages.title: Cursed Keepsake
passages.text: The keepsake has been cleansed! It is ready for a new home, where better memories can be made.

passages.title: Return to Amani'Zar
passages.text:
<name>,

Your aid is requested in Amani'Zar Village. Please meet me there.

--Liadrin

passages.title: Return to Amani'Zar
passages.text: Good, you're here.

passages.title: The Venomous Abyss: Deception Unmasked
passages.text: If my brother is no longer bowing to Malacrass, then he's in grave danger. We need to find a way to get to dem as quickly as possible. Look for anything that could let us get through de temple faster.

passages.title: Midnight: Vaults of Atal'Utek
passages.text:
Zul'jarra's forces stand watch at the gates of the Vaults of Atal'Utek, holding the line against those wicked serpents.

The fate of the entire Eastern Kingdoms rests on their blades. We would do well to provide them with reinforcements. The Children of Ula'tek are fierce, but they are no match for a seasoned <class> like you.

Traverse the temple and thin their ranks, however you can.

passages.title: Midnight: Vaults of Atal'Utek
passages.text: That should keep their numbers down, for a little while at least.

passages.title: Week 1 of 3: Gladiator's Distinction
passages.text:
Interested in training against some of our fighters? Step into the ring and show us your mettle.

Make sure you equip these medallions, and defeat at least two teams of enemies.

passages.title: Week 1 of 3: Gladiator's Distinction
passages.text: Excellent work. Always utilize your Gladiator's Medallion or you'll get crushed out there.

passages.title: Venom Fishing: My Second-Best
passages.text:
Before I send ye out hunting, ye should acquaint yerself with what remains of my crew.

Most perished in the wreck, of course. Others fell into the swamp. Some traitorous gits... well, we'll get to them in a moment, won't we?

But me loyal second mate is holding down the fort, just down river of me Landing. She'll set you up right.

passages.title: Venom Fishing: My Second-Best
passages.text: Oh, the Captain sent you? Well, isn't that a n-nice surprise.

passages.title: Into the Vaults of Atal'Utek
passages.text:
Past dis bulwark, there's nothin but snakes, spirits, and venomous death.

I've lost three lieutenants dis week. Strong ones. Brave ones. Maybe stronger and braver than you.

<Warleader Abdumati looks you over with a weary eye.>

If you want to fling yaself into de abyss, be my guest. Bring back my scouts, if you can find dem amongst de bones.

But watch your step. Dat venom will swallow you whole.

passages.title: Into the Vaults of Atal'Utek
passages.text: Don't make me send someone out to rescue you. I don't have de fighters for dat.

passages.title: Into the Vaults of Atal'Utek
passages.text:
Well... two outta three ain't bad, not for here.

You're lookin' a bit green, though. Sure dat venom didn't get to ya?

passages.title: A Curated Gift
passages.text:
I have watched the effort and care you take with the other mortals of your neighborhood, here in Razorwind Shores. This ceaseless labor on their behalf is the sort of behavior that I encourage. There's no profit to be had for you, but that isn't a driving concern for the best of your kind.

In recognition of your efforts and status, I offer you a gift. This small device contains a piece of decor for you to place in your home. I will have another for you next week.

passages.title: A Curated Gift
passages.text:
I have watched the effort and care you take with the other mortals of your neighborhood. This ceaseless labor on their behalf is the sort of behavior that I encourage. There's no profit to be had for you, but that isn't a driving concern for the best of your kind.

In recognition of your efforts and status, I offer you a gift. This small device contains a piece of decor for you to place in your home. I will have another for you next week.

passages.title: A Request from the Captain
passages.text:
Oh, uh. The Captain has requested you join him at Tokka's Landing as soon as you can.

<Second Mate Sluggs quivers in her shell.>

He had a mean look about him. Tread lightly.

passages.title: A Request from the Captain
passages.text: Ye lookin' for more work? Ye were so helpful last time.

passages.title: A Favor to the Captain
passages.text:
Oh! While you were out fishing, Captain Tokka asked to see you again. I think he's beginning to trust you.

<Second Mate Sluggs grimaces.>

The Captain's trust d-does tend to come with caveats.

passages.title: A Favor to the Captain
passages.text: I've another task for you. Each more grisly than the last, eh?

passages.title: A Plea from the Captain
passages.text:
Ohh, the Captain's really in a foul mood this time. I think you'd better go see what he wants.

<Second Mate Sluggs shakes her head.>

You're the only one who can soothe his storms, these days.

passages.title: Shoulder to Shoulder
passages.text:
De Vaults are a dangerous place. Lotta brave, headstrong fighters think dey can face de Children of Ula'tek alone. If dey're lucky, we manage to recover de bodies before dey get eaten.

I like you, adventurer. It'd be a shame to see a serpent feed you to its young. So be smart. Find people to watch your back, then carve your way through de temple together.

passages.title: Shoulder to Shoulder
passages.text: Dis is a war, <name>. No one should fight alone.

passages.title: Shoulder to Shoulder
passages.text: Shoulder to shoulder. Dat's de way we win dis battle.

passages.title: What's Out There?
passages.text:
Knowledge is de most important weapon in war. These Vaults are ancient and vast--our scouts cannot see everything. What lurks in de depths of these corrupted halls?

Dat's precisely what I need to know. Get out there and tell me what you see, but it's dangerous to go alone. You best bring some comrades if you want to make it back.

passages.title: What's Out There?
passages.text: De fiends here think dey can lurk and scheme in de dark. We will root dem out and purge dem from these lands.

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: The Altar of Corrosion
passages.text:
De Altar of Corrosion.

Who can say when dis accursed piece of stone rose out of de venom? I have studied it for lifetimes and have only just tasted its power.

<Er'inye licks her spectral lips.>

Say de word, and I will convert de corrosion you carry to something more useful. Den, you may commune with de Altar and accept its many gifts.

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: The Altar of Corrosion
passages.text: De curse claims us all in different ways.

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: The Altar of Corrosion
passages.text:
How does it feel? Unearthly? Decadent?

I would give up much to be able to taste it again for the first time.

passages.title: Autumnal Addresses
Runetotem Run
Vaults of Atal'Utek: A Toxic Tour
passages.text:
Dis temple is where all de Children of Ula'tek first crawl out of de ooze. Dis is where we hold de line.

De threat comes in waves. Sometimes short strikes. Sometimes an incursion dat overwhelms de whole temple. Sometimes a huge monstrosity rising out of de venom.

Whatever dey send, send it back cryin' to its big evil mama!

And in de meantime, do what you can to keep our patrols safe.

passages.title: Vaults of Atal'Utek: A Toxic Tour
passages.text:
You're getting a hang for de rhythm of dis awful place, eh?

Snakes crawl out of de venom pit, and we throw dem right back in.

passages.title: Bring the Ruckus
passages.text:
This place is pretty fun so far, despite all the dry political talk. I know Saltheril is trying to get the nobles to buy up war bonds, but we could really use some more energy in here. If the nobles are all asleep, no one's buying anything.

Tell you what. Go invite some of my friends. They hang out under the bridge right outside of Silvermoon's gates.

If anyone can bring some energy to the soiree, it's us.

passages.title: Bring the Ruckus
passages.text:
The energy's high, the drinks are flowing, and people are having a good time!

That's how you start making deals.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text:
The whole point of this deal is showing the nobles what we bring to the table, both for Silvermoon and for them personally.

These other groups bring strength, power, and really nice armor. What we bring is resources: getting the sin'dorei what they need, when they need it, with no questions asked.

I heard some folks over at Sunsail Anchorage have been trying out the same business, but they're putting gold in the wrong pockets. Swipe their stock and bring it here.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text: I don't mind competitors, but I don't like the deals those smugglers are making.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text: If there's anything good in these crates, we'll get it on the market.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text:
You'd be surprised at the money you can make off of weapons. No, not the kind you're meant to use--the kind you stick up on the wall and have conversations about.

Usually those weapons are expensive, or dangerous, or otherwise hard to get your hands on. The more rare and exclusive, the better.

The weapons those Twilight cultists are carrying around should sell pretty well, especially to buyers with edgier tastes. If you happen to come across any, I'll gladly take them off your hands.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text: If it has some blood on it, that's actually better.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text: Nice work. Eversong is safer because of your heroism, and I get to pocket a little more gold. I'd call that a win-win.

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
Don't let the austere demeanor fool you. Nobles are just as susceptible to flashy party favors as the rest of us.

I had my people bring over a batch of Felo'melorn replicas. They look great on display, and even better--they're enchanted. Swing them around and they leave a trail of fire.

I haven't sold an enchanted batch before, so I'd like to do some testing before I hand them out. Saltheril wouldn't be too happy if I burned a guest to a crisp.

Wanna take one of the replicas for a test run?

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
I recommend trying it out on something not flammable.

Or extremely flammable. Up to you.

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
I told you they were flashy!

Sounds like the enchantment could get tuned down a little bit, but where's the fun in that?

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text:
I feel like I just got here and I'm already fresh out of half the poisons I brought.

What? Don't look at me like that. Nobles are some of my top customers for poisons. Quieter than magic and cleaner than blades.

I need to restock. The frogs way down in the south produce a poisonous slime that I can bottle without much fuss. Bring some of it to me and I'll get you a cut of the earnings.

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text: Were you able to find any of those frogs?

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text:
Excellent. That's enough to restock what I've sold and then some.

Oh, by the way, you probably want to wash your hands. Maybe a few times.

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text:
We've been making friends with some of the guests by teaching them how to play dice. It's a nice way to draw people out of the crowd and get them in a quieter space where you can talk privately.

I wasn't expecting so much interest, to be honest. We're running out of dice sets.

I can carve some more, but I'll need materials. Usually teeth or bone are good picks. Actually, the fangs from those naga along the coast would be perfect. Now that's a conversation starter!

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text: Any luck finding some of those fangs?

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text:
Oh, that smell is... very fishy. Definitely going to let these dry out for a while.

Your exceptionally efficient help is appreciated, <name>.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text:
I talked to some of the servants earlier and it sounds like the casks are running low. That's a recipe for disaster at an event like this.

Fortunately, I've got a lot of contacts across Eversong who can help us restock.

I need to stay here and play politics, but could you head over to Tranquillien and grab a few bottles? I'll give you a list.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text: Trust me. Everything on that list is fantastic.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text: Nice work. I'll see about getting those casks refilled, but these bottles should keep everyone happy in the meantime.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text:
The oldest trick in the book is to create a problem on purpose, solve it yourself, and look like the hero.

One of the nobles just got word that some prized valuable was stolen from their estate while they were occupied here. It just so happens I might have put one of their servants up to it.

Go talk to a man named Seridis over at the livery. He'll hand over the valuable to you, then you'll come back here and pretend you valiantly subdued the thief and retrieved the item.

Everyone's happy.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text: Making friends with the servants in noble households opens up a lot of doors. Sometimes literally.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text:
Look at that. Everyone comes out a winner!

The noble gets his valuable back unscathed, Seridis gets paid handsomely, and you and I look brave and capable in front of the soiree.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text:
Gorebarb is a creature quite unlike most others who make Harandar their home. He's incredibly violent and his kind is not seen here very often. 

Let's see less of him. Kill him and bring me his pincers as proof of the deed.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text: Take care that Gorebarb doesn't catch you with those pincers. I imagine his breath isn't pleasant at all.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text: Well, well. You managed to take down Gorebarb and retrieve the pincers? Ah, of course I never doubted you would.

passages.title: WANTED: Dionaea's Thorntusks
passages.text:
Many thornmaws make the mire their home, but none as are vicious as Dionaea. Unlike the others, she kills merely for the joy of it, and her gluttony threatens the delicate balance of the wildlife in this area. 

Take her out and restore the equilibrium. Bring me back her thorntusks as proof of the deed.

passages.title: WANTED: Dionaea's Thorntusks
